opening.title: The bus
opening.summary: The team bus is leaving. Mirembe is still at the gate.
paragraphs: The bus door folds shut as Mirembe reaches the school gate. She waves. The driver sees her in the mirror, but the bus is already joining the road to Wankulukuku.

Her phone is hot in her hand. One live stream became another; she missed three calls from captain Amina and the fifteen-minute warning she herself set. Today is the district semifinal. She has trained for the starting spot since January.
Amina calls again. Behind her voice, the whole team is arguing about who will play on Mirembe’s wing. At the gate, a boda rider asks, “Sister, are we chasing that bus or just admiring it?”
The coach will hear an explanation before kickoff. Mirembe has about ten seconds to decide which one.
Uncle Rwamiti is helping with the team transport.

choices.label: Tell Amina exactly why you missed the bus.
Say you were delayed in traffic and ask them to wait.
Take the boda and explain when you arrive.

truth.title: The honest call
truth.summary: “I was on my phone,” Mirembe says. There is a pause long enough to hear Amina tell the driver to keep going. The bus cannot turn back; the t
paragraphs: “I was on my phone,” Mirembe says. There is a pause long enough to hear Amina tell the driver to keep going. The bus cannot turn back; the team has a check-in time.

Amina is annoyed, but she stays on the line. Rita, the reserve winger, has already put on Mirembe’s bib. “She deserves a chance,” Amina says. “Coach says you can still come. You will start on the bench.”

Mirembe knows how Rita cuts inside onto her right foot. She also knows the opposing fullback always follows the first run and leaves space behind her. She wants her starting place back. She is not sure she can cheer for the girl who has it. Amina asks, “So, are you coming?”

Uncle Rwamiti, helping with the match transport, is still at the gate with the water carrier the team forgot. He offers Mirembe a lift with it. “They have left their winger and their drinking water. An ambitious formation.” Going now means arriving in front of everyone carrying the bottles, with Rita already in her place. Staying means missing whatever Rita does with it.

choices.label: Go and help Rita read the game from the touchline.
Go and ask the coach to put you back in the starting side.
Stay at school; face the team at Tuesday training.

excuse.title: The traffic story
excuse.summary: “Traffic,” Mirembe says. Amina repeats it to the coach. The driver has passed the junction, so nobody waits. But the coach texts that a late
paragraphs: “Traffic,” Mirembe says. Amina repeats it to the coach. The driver has passed the junction, so nobody waits. But the coach texts that a late player can still make the bench if she arrives before halftime.
A minute later, Rita sends a photo of the team sheet. Beside Mirembe’s name someone has written DELAYED. Rita adds, “Hope you’re okay. I can start if you need me to.”
The message is kind. That makes it harder. If Mirembe keeps the story, Amina will have to back it up when the coach asks where she was. The boda rider is still at the gate.

Amina says she has already repeated the traffic explanation to the coach. Uncle Rwamiti is checking the departure sheet at the gate. He heard the calls ringing while Mirembe watched the stream, but has not spoken to Amina. Mirembe can still correct the account herself. If she lets it stand, her captain will be answering questions about a road she never used.

choices.label: Correct the story with Amina and the coach now.
Keep the traffic story and get to the ground.
Ask Rita to cover for you, then tell her the truth.

chase.title: The ride
chase.summary: The boda catches the bus at a red light, then loses it near the market. Mirembe pays the rider with the money she had saved for lunch. She r
paragraphs: The boda catches the bus at a red light, then loses it near the market. Mirembe pays the rider with the money she had saved for lunch. She reaches the ground as the teams are lining up.
Rita is on the pitch. Amina spots Mirembe at the gate and waves her over. “Coach thinks you were sick,” she says. “I guessed. I had to tell him something.”
Mirembe can still be named as a substitute. The coach is walking toward her, holding the team sheet. Amina looks relieved to see her and worried about what she might say.

The rider wants UGX 8,000. Mirembe pays from the money she kept for lunch and asks him to take the normal route, not race the bus. Uncle Rwamiti is unloading water when she reaches the ground. He points her toward the coach without making an announcement. Amina has already explained her absence; Rita is warming up in her bib. Arriving has solved only the distance.

choices.label: Tell the coach what happened and accept the bench.
Let Amina’s illness story stand and ask to substitute.
Stay off the team sheet and watch Rita’s first half.

truth_team.title: The touchline
truth_team.summary: Mirembe arrives as Rita loses the ball twice to the same defender. At the water break, she tells Rita about the space behind the fullback. R
paragraphs: Mirembe arrives as Rita loses the ball twice to the same defender. At the water break, she tells Rita about the space behind the fullback. Rita rolls her eyes—then tries it. Her cross makes the winning goal.

Mirembe does not play a minute. On the bus home, Rita shares her chapati and asks Mirembe to show her the move at training. Amina saves her a seat. The missed match is still missed, but it is no longer the only thing that happened today.

At Tuesday training, the coach pairs Mirembe and Rita on the same wing. They argue about who runs first, then discover a move neither could have made alone. Mirembe leaves her phone in the kit bag for the forty minutes they need to get it right.

truth_play.title: The bench
truth_play.summary: The coach hears Mirembe out and leaves Rita in the starting side. “You can help us in the second half,” he says. Mirembe spends the first ha
paragraphs: The coach hears Mirembe out and leaves Rita in the starting side. “You can help us in the second half,” he says. Mirembe spends the first half counting Rita’s mistakes instead of watching the opposing fullback.

When she finally comes on, she nearly scores, but rushes the shot. The team wins narrowly. Rita is polite afterward. Mirembe gets her minutes and a week to decide whether being selected was the only thing she came for.

At the next match, the coach starts Rita again and asks Mirembe to watch the opposition before she goes on. This time Mirembe tells Rita what she sees. She still wants her starting place back, and now she has a better way to earn it.

truth_leave.title: The empty pitch
truth_leave.summary: Mirembe walks back across the empty school pitch. She follows the score through Amina’s messages, then switches her phone face down. Rita sc
paragraphs: Mirembe walks back across the empty school pitch. She follows the score through Amina’s messages, then switches her phone face down. Rita scores the winner. Amina calls after the match; Mirembe lets it ring once before answering.
“We needed you there,” Amina says. “Even on the bench.” Mirembe thought staying away would spare her the embarrassment. It has also made next training feel farther away.

On Tuesday Mirembe arrives before anyone else. She has to walk past Rita and Amina to reach the pitch. Amina hands her a ball without a speech. The pass is harder to receive than an apology would have been, so Mirembe asks Rita how the winning goal happened.

excuse_correct.title: The correction
excuse_correct.summary: Mirembe sends one message to both Amina and the coach: she was on her phone, missed the bus, and let Amina repeat an excuse. Amina replies w
paragraphs: Mirembe sends one message to both Amina and the coach: she was on her phone, missed the bus, and let Amina repeat an excuse. Amina replies with a single, furious full stop. The coach tells her to report to the bench.

At halftime Mirembe helps Rita spot the open space. After the win, Amina is still angry, but she no longer has to remember which version she told. “Next time,” she says, “set an alarm that insults you.” Mirembe laughs before she can help it.

At training, Amina changes Mirembe’s contact name to “Traffic.” It lasts one day. The coach keeps Rita in the starting side for the next fixture, and Mirembe stays to help plan the wing play instead of insisting that one honest message should erase a missed bus.

excuse_keep.title: The story grows
excuse_keep.summary: Mirembe reaches the ground before halftime and comes on with twelve minutes left. She makes the pass that starts the winning move. The coach
paragraphs: Mirembe reaches the ground before halftime and comes on with twelve minutes left. She makes the pass that starts the winning move. The coach praises her for fighting through the “traffic.” Amina does not look at her.
On Monday the coach asks Amina which road was blocked so he can adjust the next departure. Mirembe’s good pass is real. So is the second explanation she now has to invent.

When Amina will not back up the invented roadblock, Mirembe tells the coach the truth herself. He is angry about the false report as much as the late arrival. She keeps her place in the squad, but the next team sheet has Rita’s name where hers used to be.

excuse_friend.title: The favour
excuse_friend.summary: Rita reads Mirembe’s confession and types for a long time. “I won’t lie to Coach,” she finally replies. “Come anyway.” Mirembe arrives to fi
paragraphs: Rita reads Mirembe’s confession and types for a long time. “I won’t lie to Coach,” she finally replies. “Come anyway.” Mirembe arrives to find Rita starting and Amina upset that both of them knew more than she did.

Mirembe tells the coach herself before halftime. She sits out, then cheers when Rita scores. Rita accepts the cheer. She does not immediately accept the apology for asking her to carry a secret before her first big match.

Rita asks Mirembe to practise crosses with her after school. She will not cover a lie again. Mirembe agrees to both terms. The first pass is clumsy; by the tenth they are laughing at how long it took them to ask one another for help.

chase_confess.title: The late arrival
chase_confess.summary: Mirembe tells the coach about the phone and corrects Amina’s guess. He puts her on the bench. Amina mutters, “You could have warned me.” Mir
paragraphs: Mirembe tells the coach about the phone and corrects Amina’s guess. He puts her on the bench. Amina mutters, “You could have warned me.” Mirembe admits she should have.

Late in the second half, the coach sends Mirembe on. She sets up Rita for a shot that goes just wide. They lose on penalties. On the ride back, the coach asks both girls to stay after training Tuesday. Neither knows if that is good news.

Tuesday’s meeting is a short one. The coach says the late arrival cost the team preparation, not just a player. Mirembe asks to help organise the next departure. Amina says she may, provided she is the first person at the bus.

chase_hide.title: The wrong seat
chase_hide.summary: “Feeling better?” the coach asks. Mirembe nods. She comes on after halftime and wins a corner, but Amina has to repeat the illness story to
paragraphs: “Feeling better?” the coach asks. Mirembe nods. She comes on after halftime and wins a corner, but Amina has to repeat the illness story to the team manager when the attendance sheet comes around.

The team wins. Amina celebrates with everyone else, then hands Mirembe the sheet. “You sign it,” she says. Mirembe has made it to the match. She has also handed her captain a problem that followed them home.

Amina refuses to sign a false attendance note. Mirembe corrects it herself the next morning. The coach removes her from one training match, then asks her to lead the warm-up the following week. Amina watches whether she arrives on time.

chase_watch.title: The last whistle
chase_watch.summary: Mirembe tells the coach she arrived too late to be listed. He asks her to carry water to the far touchline. From there she sees the defender
paragraphs: Mirembe tells the coach she arrived too late to be listed. He asks her to carry water to the far touchline. From there she sees the defender leaving space. She shouts it to Rita, who nods and nearly scores.

They lose 1–0. Rita thanks her anyway. On the walk out, the coach asks why she was late. Mirembe finally answers. “All right,” he says. “Tuesday, then.” It is neither forgiveness nor a ban. It is a place to begin.

Mirembe returns Tuesday with no claim that her shouted advice would have won the semifinal. Rita asks her to demonstrate the run she spotted. They try it until the light goes. The loss remains theirs; so does the next training session.

opening.title: Final whistle
opening.summary: Joel has lost the trip money. The next match starts in eight minutes.
paragraphs: The final whistle sounds from the television in the kiosk. Joel’s betting slip is worthless. The UGX 20,000 he used belongs to the class trip collection, and the class representative is waiting for it across the road.

He is seventeen. He made the first bet yesterday with his own pocket money, won, and told himself he had found an easy way to add to the trip fund. This morning’s loss took the whole amount. His friend Ssentongo points at the next match on the screen. “One goal and you recover everything.”
The mobile money agent beside the kiosk is counting cash. Joel’s cousin has offered him a small loan before. The class representative waves from the school gate.

choices.label: Use the last UGX 10,000 in his wallet on the next match.
Ask his cousin for a loan before the collection closes.
Tell the class representative what happened.

bet.title: The next slip
bet.summary: Joel places the second bet. The team he chose scores early. For twenty minutes he can almost feel the lost money back in his hand. Then the
paragraphs: Joel places the second bet. The team he chose scores early. For twenty minutes he can almost feel the lost money back in his hand. Then the equaliser comes. His ticket now pays nothing.
Ssentongo says a live bet can still fix it if Joel borrows a stake. The agent asks whether he is buying airtime or sending money. Joel looks at the empty place in his wallet where his bus fare was.
Uncle Rwamiti: “The next match has not agreed to repay the last one.”

choices.label: Stop betting and explain the missing collection.
Borrow a stake from Ssentongo for one last attempt.

borrow.title: The loan
borrow.summary: His cousin Mariam sends UGX 20,000 after Joel says he is short for a school trip. “Pay me Friday,” she writes. The collection is covered, bu
paragraphs: His cousin Mariam sends UGX 20,000 after Joel says he is short for a school trip. “Pay me Friday,” she writes. The collection is covered, but Mariam thinks it is a temporary cash shortage.

Mariam calls as Joel reaches Faridah. She had planned to use the UGX 20,000 for stall stock tomorrow. “Friday, eh? I am writing it down.” Faridah says the collection closes in five minutes. Returning the loan now would leave his trip unpaid; keeping it will leave Mariam short until he earns it.
Uncle Rwamiti: “Friday has arrived in the chat before the money has left the till.”

choices.label: Explain the loss and ask Mariam to agree to stall work as repayment.
Pay the collection now and keep the reason from Mariam until Friday.

tell.title: The collection
tell.summary: Joel tells class representative Faridah he used the UGX 20,000 and lost it. She does not shout. She takes out the collection sheet and cross
paragraphs: Joel tells class representative Faridah he used the UGX 20,000 and lost it. She does not shout. She takes out the collection sheet and crosses off his name. “I have to balance this before the teacher comes,” she says.

The teacher is ten minutes away. Faridah offers to walk in with him, but she will not say the money was misplaced. Joel’s mother has already paid for his trip once. He can call her, or ask the teacher for time to earn it back.
Uncle Rwamiti: “The collection sheet has a line for the amount. Joel is finding his name on it.”

choices.label: Ask the teacher for a repayment plan with Faridah present.
Call his mother before the teacher contacts her.

bet_stop.title: The cash box
bet_stop.summary: Joel tells Faridah about both losses. She writes UGX 20,000 beside his name, not UGX 30,000. “Your own fare is your own headache,” she says.
paragraphs: Joel tells Faridah about both losses. She writes UGX 20,000 beside his name, not UGX 30,000. “Your own fare is your own headache,” she says. He misses the trip deadline and spends Saturday helping his uncle deliver crates to repay the fund.
Ssentongo sends him the score of the next match. Joel reads it once, then puts the phone away. He is still angry that he cannot go. At least the number he owes has stopped moving.

On the class trip day, Joel sees photos from the bus while carrying crates. He is tempted to say the work is unfair. Faridah sends a message confirming the final repayment, and he saves that receipt instead of the match scores.

bet_more.title: The borrowed stake
bet_more.summary: Ssentongo lends him UGX 10,000 for one final stake. The bet loses. Joel now owes the trip collection UGX 20,000 and Ssentongo UGX 10,000; hi
paragraphs: Ssentongo lends him UGX 10,000 for one final stake. The bet loses. Joel now owes the trip collection UGX 20,000 and Ssentongo UGX 10,000; his own UGX 10,000 bus fare is also gone.

Ssentongo tells Faridah before Joel does. The trip becomes a meeting with the teacher, Ssentongo, and two different amounts written on paper. Joel had tried to keep one person from finding out; he now has to speak to three.

Ssentongo gets his loan back first because he asks loudest. Faridah is still short. Joel tells the teacher both amounts and helps draw up separate repayments, rather than making another friend carry the missing trip money in silence.

borrow_truth.title: The conversation
borrow_truth.summary: Joel explains the bet before handing the cash to Faridah. Mariam is quiet long enough for him to hear her calculator. She agrees to two week
paragraphs: Joel explains the bet before handing the cash to Faridah. Mariam is quiet long enough for him to hear her calculator. She agrees to two weekend shifts at the stall instead of a Friday cash repayment. He pays the collection with her agreement.

He goes on the trip. On Saturday Mariam gives him the sales book and keeps the cash drawer herself. They stock fewer items that first weekend because her UGX 20,000 is still tied up in him. A customer wants a size they do not have; Joel has to say it.

His two shifts settle the loan. Mariam writes PAID beside his name, then asks him to finish stacking the crates before leaving. The trip photograph is on his phone. The stock he helped count is back on her shelves.

borrow_hide.title: The promise
borrow_hide.summary: Joel pays Faridah and goes on the trip without telling Mariam about the bet. On Friday he has earned nothing. Mariam had ordered stock expec
paragraphs: Joel pays Faridah and goes on the trip without telling Mariam about the bet. On Friday he has earned nothing. Mariam had ordered stock expecting the repayment; she phones while the supplier waits beside her stall.

Joel tells her the money is still missing and admits why. She cancels part of the order, losing the reduced bulk price. She will accept repayment in instalments, but says she cannot give him work this weekend: the smaller delivery needs no extra pair of hands.

He earns the UGX 20,000 through errands elsewhere and sends each instalment by mobile money. Mariam acknowledges the last transfer with “Received.” When he asks for fare another week, she gives him the taxi route instead.

tell_plan.title: The repayment
tell_plan.summary: The teacher agrees to two weeks for repayment and asks Joel to sign the collection sheet with the amount owed. He will not travel unless it
paragraphs: The teacher agrees to two weeks for repayment and asks Joel to sign the collection sheet with the amount owed. He will not travel unless it is settled before departure. Faridah has a record that protects her from carrying his shortage.

Joel spends Saturday setting up chairs for a neighbourhood event and earns UGX 10,000. The teacher has allowed repayment time, not a place on the departing bus. Faridah records the instalment while his classmates load their bags.

Faridah marks the collection paid only when the last instalment arrives. Joel asks to see the sheet and checks his own name. The trip has gone without him, but he can face the class representative without inventing a new score.

tell_friend.title: The phone call
tell_friend.summary: His mother answers from a taxi. Joel gets through the whole story before she speaks. She pays Faridah directly, then tells Joel the trip mon
paragraphs: His mother answers from a taxi. Joel gets through the whole story before she speaks. She pays Faridah directly, then tells Joel the trip money will come out of the money she had set aside for his new boots.
He goes on the trip in his old pair. They are not comfortable. His mother still asks for a photograph from the bus. Joel sends one and, for once, leaves the football scores unopened.

When he asks his mother about the boots weeks later, she says they can save again. She does not replace the money immediately. Joel starts putting aside a little from errands; the boots will take longer than a lucky Saturday.

opening.title: The birthday
opening.summary: At a birthday gathering, Asha’s friend is suddenly struggling to stay awake.
paragraphs: Asha finds Leila sitting on the back steps of the birthday house, blinking slowly while music shakes the window behind her. Ten minutes ago Leila had been laughing. Now she cannot finish a sentence.

Leila says someone gave her something to try. She does not know exactly what it was. A boy from the party says she only needs water and asks Asha not to make trouble. Asha is sixteen; Leila is her oldest friend. Leila’s mother will be furious if she hears about this.
Asha tries Leila’s name again. Leila answers, but her eyes close before the last word. The host’s aunt is inside. A nearby clinic is still open.
Uncle Rwamiti is helping the host arrange chairs.

choices.label: Call Leila’s mother and tell her what Asha knows.
Bring the host’s aunt to Leila immediately.
Phone the nearby clinic for immediate guidance.

mother.title: The call
mother.summary: Leila’s mother answers on the second ring. She asks where they are and says she is coming. When Asha describes Leila’s breathing and drowsin
paragraphs: Leila’s mother answers on the second ring. She asks where they are and says she is coming. When Asha describes Leila’s breathing and drowsiness, her voice changes: “Do not wait for me. Get an adult and medical help now.”
Leila hears her mother’s name and grabs Asha’s wrist. “You promised,” she whispers. Asha remembers promising not to tell anyone about a different, harmless secret last week. This is not that secret.

Uncle Rwamiti has been carrying chairs at the birthday house. When he sees Asha trying to hear the call, he switches off the nearest speaker and keeps curious guests inside. Leila’s mother asks what happened before the call. Asha knows what she saw and what Leila said; she does not know what was taken. Now she has to give an account without filling the gaps.

choices.label: Ask the host’s aunt to arrange immediate care and stay with Leila.
Take Leila toward the clinic with the aunt and meet her mother there.

host.title: The host
host.summary: The host’s aunt turns off the music near the steps and checks on Leila. She calls the clinic and asks two guests what Leila took. Their stor
paragraphs: The host’s aunt turns off the music near the steps and checks on Leila. She calls the clinic and asks two guests what Leila took. Their stories do not match. One says a tablet; another says she only drank from a bottle.
The aunt says they need professional help and asks Asha to call Leila’s family. A boy says everyone at the party will be blamed if Asha does. Leila is too drowsy to settle the argument.

Uncle Rwamiti opens the gate while the aunt arranges help. The host starts explaining which guests might have brought something; the aunt asks him to write what he actually saw. Asha realises the adults have different pieces of the evening. Someone still has to contact Leila’s family, and someone who was beside her has to stay available to answer questions.

choices.label: Call Leila’s mother while the aunt arranges care.
Go with the aunt and ask her to contact the family.

clinic.title: The nurse
clinic.summary: A nurse asks whether Leila is awake and breathing normally. Asha answers as best she can. The nurse tells her to get immediate medical help
paragraphs: A nurse asks whether Leila is awake and breathing normally. Asha answers as best she can. The nurse tells her to get immediate medical help and an adult at the house; guesses about what Leila took are not enough.
When Asha returns to the steps, Leila is trying to stand. The boy who offered water says the clinic call was an overreaction. The host’s aunt comes to the door after hearing her name.

Uncle Rwamiti takes the aunt’s bags while she helps Leila, leaving Asha free to speak. A party guest asks whether she is about to name everyone. That is not what the nurse asked. Asha can describe Leila’s words and the change she noticed without turning guesses about the party into facts. Leila squeezes her hand, still frightened of what her mother will hear.

choices.label: Tell the aunt and nurse everything Asha observed.
Ask the aunt to help, but first honour Leila’s request to keep the substance private.

mother_stay.title: The doorway
mother_stay.summary: The aunt calls for help and stays with Leila while Asha keeps talking to her. Her mother arrives before they leave for the clinic. She is fr
paragraphs: The aunt calls for help and stays with Leila while Asha keeps talking to her. Her mother arrives before they leave for the clinic. She is frightened, not interested in the party’s excuses.
After Leila has been assessed, she refuses to look at Asha for a while. Two days later she sends a message: “Still angry. Also, thank you.” Asha lets both sentences be true.

At school, Leila asks Asha not to tell their friends the details. Asha agrees and tells the curious ones only that Leila got help and is back. Their friendship returns in ordinary pieces: a shared seat, a borrowed pen, a joke that makes both of them laugh too loudly.

mother_go.title: The ride
mother_go.summary: The aunt arranges transport to the clinic. Asha goes with Leila and gives the nurse what she knows, including what she does not. Leila’s mot
paragraphs: The aunt arranges transport to the clinic. Asha goes with Leila and gives the nurse what she knows, including what she does not. Leila’s mother meets them there carrying one slipper in her hand; she left home too quickly to find the other.
Leila recovers. Later she asks Asha why she called her mother. “I was scared,” Asha says. It is the first honest answer either of them has given about that night.

Leila’s mother later thanks Asha for giving the nurse the uncertain account instead of pretending to know what was taken. Asha still hears the frightened voice from that call. Leila asks her to come over for tea, where they speak about the party without an audience.

host_help.title: The grown-up
host_help.summary: Leila’s mother comes straight to the clinic. The aunt gives the nurse the two conflicting accounts instead of choosing the one that sounds l
paragraphs: Leila’s mother comes straight to the clinic. The aunt gives the nurse the two conflicting accounts instead of choosing the one that sounds less alarming. Asha stays with Leila until the assessment is done.
The host apologises for trying to keep the party quiet. Leila is embarrassed to face everyone, so Asha walks her out by the side gate. The birthday photos circulate. Neither girl appears in them.
The host’s aunt checks in once after Leila is home. Asha lets Leila answer the message herself. It is a small courtesy after a night when every adult had to make quick decisions around her.

host_wait.title: The noise
host_wait.summary: The aunt gets Leila to care promptly and contacts her family on the way. Asha has left the call to someone older. At the clinic, Leila’s mot
paragraphs: The aunt gets Leila to care promptly and contacts her family on the way. Asha has left the call to someone older. At the clinic, Leila’s mother asks Asha what she noticed first. The question catches her: she had noticed more than she told the aunt.
Leila is okay. Asha answers fully now, including the moment Leila could not finish a sentence. She learns that handing a problem to an adult does not mean her own observations cease to matter.

Asha writes down the first signs she noticed while they are fresh, in case Leila wants to understand the evening later. She shows Leila the note, not the class group. Leila keeps it and says she will decide what to do with it.

clinic_now.title: The assessment
clinic_now.summary: The aunt and Asha tell the nurse the sequence: laughter, confusion, drowsiness, and the uncertain account of what Leila took. The nurse take
paragraphs: The aunt and Asha tell the nurse the sequence: laughter, confusion, drowsiness, and the uncertain account of what Leila took. The nurse takes over. Leila’s mother is called while the assessment begins.
On the way home, Asha’s phone is full of party gossip. She gives nobody a diagnosis she does not have. She can speak for what she saw, and leaves Leila to tell the rest when she is ready.

The nurse’s questions were more useful than the guests’ confident guesses. Asha remembers that when a rumour names the person who gave Leila something. She refuses to add a name she never saw and leaves the account with the people treating Leila.

clinic_secret.title: The promise
clinic_secret.summary: Asha tells the aunt that Leila is very drowsy but leaves out what Leila said about trying something. At the clinic, the nurse asks directly.
paragraphs: Asha tells the aunt that Leila is very drowsy but leaves out what Leila said about trying something. At the clinic, the nurse asks directly. Asha looks at Leila, who can barely keep her eyes open, and gives the full account.

The delay has made the explanation harder, not the care less important. Later Leila says she wishes Asha had spoken sooner. Asha agrees, though she had thought silence was the kinder way to be a friend.

Asha apologises for the part she held back. Leila says she had asked for silence because she was frightened of her mother, not because she knew what was safe. They disagree about the party and agree that neither wants to be left guessing if it happens again.

opening.title: The transfer
opening.summary: A mobile money transfer arrives by mistake just as Brian’s aunt needs rent.
paragraphs: Brian’s phone vibrates beside his aunt’s vegetable stall in Kalerwe. UGX 500,000 has arrived by mobile money. He was expecting UGX 5,000 from a customer, not this.

A man calls immediately and says he sent it to the wrong number. He sounds frightened. Brian is seventeen and has never held that much money. His aunt’s landlord has given her until six o’clock to pay rent on the stall. Brian can see the envelope of smaller notes she has been counting all morning.
The caller offers to pay Brian a little for his trouble if he sends the money straight back to a different number. The agent next door is open. The landlord turns into the market lane.
Uncle Rwamiti collects empty crates from the stall on his delivery round.

choices.label: Ask the agent to verify the transfer and the safe way to reverse it.
Tell his aunt about the money before acting.
Keep the money untouched and question the caller first.

verify.title: The agent
verify.summary: The agent checks the transaction reference but refuses to handle Brian’s PIN or send to a new number. The original sender has already filed
paragraphs: The agent checks the transaction reference but refuses to handle Brian’s PIN or send to a new number. The original sender has already filed a reversal request. It may take time.

Outside, the landlord asks Brian’s aunt for the balance. The caller rings again and says he needs the money before a hospital payment closes. Brian cannot prove his story, but the urgency in his voice is real.

Uncle Rwamiti stops at the stall with two empty crates. The landlord asks him whether the afternoon delivery can wait. It can, but the supplier will not hold tomorrow’s price. Brian’s aunt starts counting her own cash for the half-rent payment. Returning the transfer leaves the stall short of stock; waiting at the agent leaves her short of someone to help sell what remains.

choices.label: Follow the verified reversal process and tell his aunt why it may take time.
Ask the agent to hold the case while Brian looks for the sender in person.

aunt.title: The rent
aunt.summary: His aunt reads the message twice. “That is the stall rent,” she says, then corrects herself: “That is somebody’s money.” She asks Brian to c
paragraphs: His aunt reads the message twice. “That is the stall rent,” she says, then corrects herself: “That is somebody’s money.” She asks Brian to call the agent and verify the transaction.

The landlord arrives and offers an extension if she can pay half today. His aunt could cover the half from her own sales, leaving little to buy stock tomorrow. She asks Brian what the caller said about the different number.

Uncle Rwamiti has come for the empty crates and offers to take her payment to the supplier. She counts the notes, stops, and tells him to wait. Brian sees that paying half the rent from her own money will leave less for tomorrow’s stock. The extra balance on his phone looks like an answer again. His aunt asks him to stay while she makes the calls.

choices.label: Tell the landlord they can pay half and use the official reversal.
Let his aunt use part of the transfer and plan to replace it next week.

wait.title: The caller
wait.summary: Brian asks the caller for the transaction reference. The number matches the message. Then the caller asks for Brian’s PIN “to speed things u
paragraphs: Brian asks the caller for the transaction reference. The number matches the message. Then the caller asks for Brian’s PIN “to speed things up.” Brian ends the call. A second number sends a message claiming to be support.
The money is still in Brian’s wallet. The real sender may be trying to recover it, but these calls give him no safe way to know who is speaking. His aunt needs to buy stock before the market closes.

Uncle Rwamiti asks Brian to help lift the last crate onto the stall. “This one is ours,” his aunt says, checking the invoice before she pays him. It is a joke until Brian looks back at his phone. The landlord and supplier both want answers today. He has money available on the screen and still no permission to treat it as the stall’s float.

choices.label: Take the reference to the agent and request a traced reversal.
Use some money for stock while waiting for the claim to be sorted.

verify_return.title: The reversal
verify_return.summary: The agent confirms the official reversal request. Brian does not share his PIN or send to a third number. His aunt pays half the rent from h
paragraphs: The agent confirms the official reversal request. Brian does not share his PIN or send to a third number. His aunt pays half the rent from her own notes and gets three more days.
The reversal clears the next afternoon. Brian still helps his aunt find the remaining rent. The extra money had arrived at the exact moment they needed it; its timing did not make it theirs.

Three days later Brian’s aunt finds the rest of the rent through sales and a smaller loan she records in her own book. Brian helps count the tomatoes twice. The caller’s money is gone from his wallet, but the problem in front of them has a name and a date.

verify_delay.title: The queue
verify_delay.summary: The agent cannot identify the caller in person from the reference. Brian waits at the stall hoping the man will appear. By closing time, the
paragraphs: The agent cannot identify the caller in person from the reference. Brian waits at the stall hoping the man will appear. By closing time, the reversal request is still pending and the landlord has gone.

His aunt asks why Brian spent the afternoon chasing a stranger instead of helping sell vegetables. He tells her the whole story. They begin the official process that evening, after losing the best market hours.

The sender’s official request eventually clears. Brian learns that waiting in person gave him no better proof than the transaction record. His aunt has him make up the lost market hours on Saturday, when the stall is busiest.

aunt_open.title: The rent call
aunt_open.summary: His aunt pays half with her sales and asks for the extension. The landlord writes the new date on the receipt. Brian submits the reversal re
paragraphs: His aunt pays half with her sales and asks for the extension. The landlord writes the new date on the receipt. Brian submits the reversal request at the agent while she closes the stall.
The next morning the caller sends a brief thank-you. His aunt does not ask for a reward. She does ask Brian to help count stock, because honest decisions still leave rent to pay.

The landlord returns on the date written on the receipt. Brian’s aunt pays the balance without asking Brian to explain the wrong transfer again. Instead she asks him to call out each sale; he is finally trusted with ordinary cash.

aunt_use.title: The receipt
aunt_use.summary: His aunt uses UGX 200,000 toward the rent and promises to replace it after the weekend market. The official reversal request freezes Brian’s
paragraphs: His aunt uses UGX 200,000 toward the rent and promises to replace it after the weekend market. The official reversal request freezes Brian’s wallet before those sales arrive. Now the caller’s money and the stall’s working cash are tangled.
They repay it with help from an uncle and spend the week with less stock. Brian’s aunt says she thought borrowing for a day would be harmless. Brian had thought the same; neither had asked the owner.

For a month Brian’s aunt writes every stall expense in a notebook, including the discount sale. Brian asks her to leave the UGX 200,000 line visible. It is not a family shame to erase; it is how they remember what the quick decision cost.

wait_trace.title: The sender
wait_trace.summary: The agent confirms the transfer and starts the official reversal. The second “support” number stops calling when Brian says he is at an agen
paragraphs: The agent confirms the transfer and starts the official reversal. The second “support” number stops calling when Brian says he is at an agent. The first caller sends a message with a relieved thank-you after the money returns.
Brian tells his aunt about the near mistake. She says, “You kept your PIN and somebody else’s cash. That is enough excitement for one Tuesday.” Then she hands him a crate of tomatoes.

The agent later points out that the second caller was never part of the transfer record. Brian saves the official receipt and blocks the other number. At the stall, his aunt jokes that she would prefer their next surprise to be a customer buying a whole crate.

wait_spend.title: The shortfall
wait_spend.summary: Brian buys stock with UGX 100,000 and keeps a note of every shilling. By the next day the reversal claim is verified. The stock has not all
paragraphs: Brian buys stock with UGX 100,000 and keeps a note of every shilling. By the next day the reversal claim is verified. The stock has not all sold. The wallet cannot return the full amount.
His aunt sells at a discount to cover the shortfall. Brian had intended to make the owner whole. The intention does not appear on the transaction record, and it cannot buy back the margin they lost.

The discounted stock sells by evening, but not at the price his aunt planned. Brian works the next two weekends to rebuild the float. The sender receives the full amount; the cost stays with the stall that briefly treated it as available.

opening.title: The voice note
opening.summary: Nadia’s class group is waiting for a voice note that could wreck a classmate’s name.
paragraphs: Nadia’s thumb hovers over Forward. A voice note in her inbox says that Grace stole scholarship application forms from the office. The recording ends just as the speaker says, “But I saw—”

The class group has already decided something happened. Someone has posted Grace’s photograph with a question mark. Nadia is sixteen, and Grace sits two desks away. Yesterday Nadia saw Grace carrying an envelope from the office, but she did not see what was inside.

The sender, her friend Pearl, says, “Put the audio there before they say we hid it.” Across the corridor Grace is heading toward the same group of students. Nadia has a few steps to choose what the group hears next.

choices.label: Ask Pearl for the uncut recording before forwarding anything.
Show Grace the message privately.
Take the note to the class representative with what Nadia actually saw.

source.title: The sender
source.summary: Pearl admits she received the clip from someone else. A longer version arrives: the speaker says Grace took the forms to the photocopy room
paragraphs: Pearl admits she received the clip from someone else. A longer version arrives: the speaker says Grace took the forms to the photocopy room after a teacher asked her to. Pearl still wants Nadia to post the clip to “clear it up.”
The class group is demanding proof. Nadia can share the full recording, but that would spread the accusation to people who have not heard it yet. Grace has reached the corridor outside.
The teacher can confirm the photocopy task tomorrow. Posting the whole audio may stop the allegation tonight, but also broadcasts a student’s private explanation to everyone who missed the cut clip.

choices.label: Ask the teacher to confirm the photocopy task and correct the rumour without reposting audio.
Post the full recording to stop the cut clip.

subject.title: The accused
subject.summary: Grace listens once and goes pale. She says the teacher asked her to carry the forms. She has a message from the teacher, but it also names a
paragraphs: Grace listens once and goes pale. She says the teacher asked her to carry the forms. She has a message from the teacher, but it also names another pupil who had missed the deadline and asked for help.

Grace wants the accusation stopped without putting that pupil’s private situation in the class group. Nadia can go with her to the teacher, or keep the voice note off the group and let Grace handle it herself.

Grace asks for the rumour to stop without putting her private explanation in the class group. You can seek a narrow correction together, or leave her to choose the timing while the messages keep arriving.

choices.label: Go with Grace to the teacher and ask for a narrow correction.
Do not forward it; let Grace decide whether to respond.

rep.title: The class rep
rep.summary: Class representative Musa listens and says the clip sounds edited. He wants to ask the teacher, but a group administrator is threatening to
paragraphs: Class representative Musa listens and says the clip sounds edited. He wants to ask the teacher, but a group administrator is threatening to post it within five minutes.

Musa asks Nadia whether she saw a theft. She says she saw an envelope. The distinction sounds small until he repeats it aloud. He can request a pause in the group, or forward the clip to the teacher and risk another copy escaping.
Musa can ask the teacher to verify. Sending him the audio gives him the evidence and another copy to contain; a description is narrower but may be questioned.

choices.label: Ask Musa to pause the group and verify with the teacher.
Send the clip to Musa to pass to the teacher.

source_check.title: The full recording
source_check.summary: The teacher confirms that Grace carried the forms to the photocopy room. Musa posts a short correction: the forms were never missing. Nadia
paragraphs: The teacher confirms that Grace carried the forms to the photocopy room. Musa posts a short correction: the forms were never missing. Nadia does not share the recording.

Pearl says the clip might have forced a faster answer. Grace says a faster answer would also have made her photograph travel farther. The group goes quiet, which is a welcome change for one afternoon.

A week later Pearl asks Nadia to check another clip. Nadia says she will, but not in the middle of a crowd with her thumb already on Forward. Pearl groans at the delay and sends the original recording anyway.

source_send.title: The leak
source_send.summary: Nadia posts the full recording with the ending that clears Grace. By lunch, people have saved only its first half and sent it to other class
paragraphs: Nadia posts the full recording with the ending that clears Grace. By lunch, people have saved only its first half and sent it to other classes. The correction is attached to some copies, not all.
Grace’s name is cleared at school. A cousin across town still messages her about “that voice note.” Nadia had shared the answer and the accusation in the same tap.

Nadia helps Grace write one clear correction that can be forwarded without the accusation attached. Some people reply; others never do. Grace chooses which conversations are worth her time, and Nadia keeps correcting copies she helped set loose.

subject_together.title: The conversation
subject_together.summary: The teacher confirms the task without naming the other pupil. Musa removes Grace’s photograph and posts the correction. Grace thanks Nadia f
paragraphs: The teacher confirms the task without naming the other pupil. Musa removes Grace’s photograph and posts the correction. Grace thanks Nadia for coming, then asks her to delete the recording.
Nadia does. On the way home Pearl complains that Grace got special treatment. Nadia tells her exactly what she saw: an envelope, not a crime.
Grace and Nadia sit together in class the next day. They are not suddenly close friends. When someone asks what “really happened,” Grace points to the teacher’s correction and goes back to her work.

subject_guard.title: The silence
subject_guard.summary: Nadia leaves the note unsent. Grace chooses not to address the group that afternoon. By evening, another student has posted the cut version
paragraphs: Nadia leaves the note unsent. Grace chooses not to address the group that afternoon. By evening, another student has posted the cut version and Grace is answering messages from people she barely knows.
Nadia sends her the teacher’s contact and offers to accompany her tomorrow. She respected Grace’s choice, but wishes she had asked how to help contain the rumour while they still had time.

The next morning Grace asks Nadia to come with her to the teacher. Nadia does. She cannot prevent every forward that went out overnight, but she can stand beside Grace while the class receives a correction from someone who knows the facts.

rep_context.title: The meeting
rep_context.summary: Musa asks the group to stop sharing the clip until the teacher checks. The administrator grumbles but pauses. The teacher confirms the forms
paragraphs: Musa asks the group to stop sharing the clip until the teacher checks. The administrator grumbles but pauses. The teacher confirms the forms were copied for a pupil who needed another copy.
Grace hears about the near accusation from Musa, not a hundred notifications. Nadia has still taken a risk by involving him; he has used the responsibility with care.

Musa writes a short record of the teacher’s answer for the class group and removes the speculation. Nadia reads it twice before sharing it with Pearl. This time there is no private voice note attached.

rep_forward.title: The screenshot
rep_forward.summary: Musa passes the note to the teacher. A screenshot of their chat, with the audio attached, reaches the group through another phone. The teach
paragraphs: Musa passes the note to the teacher. A screenshot of their chat, with the audio attached, reaches the group through another phone. The teacher clears Grace that afternoon, but the recording has escaped.
Musa apologises for leaving his screen open. Nadia cannot undo the send. She can help him correct the record in the same spaces where it spread, one awkward message at a time.

For several days Nadia and Musa ask administrators of the other groups to remove the leaked clip and post the correction. One refuses. Grace says she would rather they stop showing her every refusal. They listen to that request too.

opening.title: The message
opening.summary: Tendo and Musa both want to stay close. Neither has said what tonight means.
paragraphs: Tendo reads Musa’s message outside a café in Ntinda: “Are we still meeting tonight?” Their last conversation ended with both saying “we’ll see,” and neither asking what the other meant.

They have been dating for four months. Friends keep asking whether they have “made it official,” as if the answer belongs to the audience. Tendo is seventeen. She likes Musa. She also does not want to guess what he expects when they are alone. Last week he said he felt she did not trust him; she said she felt rushed. Then the taxi came and they left it there.
Musa is inside, holding two cups of tea. Tendo can go in, change the plan, or start the conversation by phone.

choices.label: Sit down with Musa and speak plainly before making tonight’s plan.
Keep the meeting, but choose a public place to talk first.
Postpone tonight and explain why by message.

talk.title: The café
talk.summary: Tendo says she wants to be close without being pushed into a decision about sex. Musa says he thought “we’ll see” meant she was considering
paragraphs: Tendo says she wants to be close without being pushed into a decision about sex. Musa says he thought “we’ll see” meant she was considering it tonight. He looks embarrassed, then asks what she does want.

She is relieved he asked, but notices he has not said what he wants either. They have enough time before the café closes to speak about boundaries, protection, and what each would do if either changed their mind.
Musa asks whether tonight’s invitation means what he thought it did. Tendo can state what she will agree to tonight, or hear his expectations before giving her answer. Their tea is going cold.

choices.label: Set a boundary for tonight and agree to revisit the larger question together.
Ask Musa to say what he wants and what he would take responsibility for.

meet.title: The plan
meet.summary: They move to a busy table near the window. Musa thought they were going to a friend’s empty flat later. Tendo had imagined dinner and a walk
paragraphs: They move to a busy table near the window. Musa thought they were going to a friend’s empty flat later. Tendo had imagined dinner and a walk. Both had made a plan without telling the other.
Musa says he can cancel the flat. Tendo can state her boundary here, or continue the evening and promise herself she will speak if the moment changes.
The chips arrive before the difficult question. Tendo can rule out going to the flat now, or keep dinner ordinary for a while at the cost of letting Musa assume the plan still stands.

choices.label: Tell Musa now that the flat is not part of her plan.
Continue to dinner and speak when she feels ready.

pause.title: The reply
pause.summary: Tendo writes: “I like you. I’m not ready to guess what tonight is meant to be. Can we talk?” Musa replies after several minutes: “I thought
paragraphs: Tendo writes: “I like you. I’m not ready to guess what tonight is meant to be. Can we talk?” Musa replies after several minutes: “I thought we already had.” She can call and hear what he meant, or keep the date postponed until she can explain herself clearly. The phone feels too small for the conversation, but it is where they are now.
She can call and hear what he meant, or leave the evening open and give them both room. The phone feels too small for the conversation, but it is where they are now.

Musa sends a photograph of two untouched teas. Calling now could clear up whether she is cancelling a date or ending the relationship. Keeping the postponement gives her space and leaves him with that uncertainty.

choices.label: Call him and name the question both have avoided.
Keep the date postponed and meet another day.

talk_boundary.title: The walk home
talk_boundary.summary: They agree on tea and a walk, and that neither owes the other a next step. Musa admits he was afraid asking directly would ruin the mood. Te
paragraphs: They agree on tea and a walk, and that neither owes the other a next step. Musa admits he was afraid asking directly would ruin the mood. Tendo laughs: “Your mysterious mood nearly ruined the tea.”
On the way home they disagree about where the relationship is going. It is an ordinary disagreement they can now describe, rather than one either must silently endure.

On Saturday they meet again and decide what they want to know about sexual health before any future step. Musa brings questions written in his notes app; Tendo brings some of her own. Neither mistakes preparation for a promise.

talk_listen.title: The new date
talk_listen.summary: Musa says he wants more intimacy but had not thought carefully about protection or what happens if either person says stop. He does not like
paragraphs: Musa says he wants more intimacy but had not thought carefully about protection or what happens if either person says stop. He does not like hearing himself say that. Tendo says she is not ready tonight.
They decide to seek reliable information together before making any later decision. They leave the café still a couple, without pretending the conversation is finished.

Musa later sends a link from a youth health service and asks whether Tendo wants to go together. She says yes to information, not to a deadline. Their messages become less mysterious once each understands the difference.

meet_speak.title: The doorstep
meet_speak.summary: Musa cancels the flat. He is disappointed and admits it instead of pretending otherwise. Tendo says disappointment is allowed; pressure is n
paragraphs: Musa cancels the flat. He is disappointed and admits it instead of pretending otherwise. Tendo says disappointment is allowed; pressure is not. They eat chips at the café and talk about why each guessed so badly.
At the taxi stage, Musa asks if they can meet again Saturday. Tendo says yes, but only after he promises to choose a place with better chips.

The next week Musa suggests the same café. Tendo says the conversation can continue there. He chooses a table by the window and asks before changing the plan. The question is small, and she notices it.

meet_drift.title: The stop
meet_drift.summary: Dinner is pleasant. When Musa mentions the flat again, Tendo finally says she does not want to go. He is surprised and asks why she waited.
paragraphs: Dinner is pleasant. When Musa mentions the flat again, Tendo finally says she does not want to go. He is surprised and asks why she waited. She says she was afraid of spoiling the night.
They part early, both unsettled. The boundary holds. On the ride home Tendo writes down what she wishes she had said at the first table, for the next conversation she chooses to have.

When they meet again, Tendo begins with the sentence she had written on the taxi. Musa says he had felt rejected but did not want her to agree merely to soothe him. They stay together long enough to hear what each meant.

pause_call.title: The call
pause_call.summary: Musa answers. They each explain the meaning they had put inside “we’ll see.” They do not agree about tonight, so they cancel the plan and ar
paragraphs: Musa answers. They each explain the meaning they had put inside “we’ll see.” They do not agree about tonight, so they cancel the plan and arrange a daytime meeting to talk without an audience.
The call is awkward and a little funny when Musa admits he bought two cups of tea before checking whether she was coming. He drinks both. Neither calls the other cruel for needing time.

At their daytime meeting, neither arrives with a verdict. They agree that being a couple does not settle each decision in advance. Musa asks if they can still disagree without assuming the relationship is ending; Tendo says that is what she hopes they are learning.

pause_silence.title: The space
pause_silence.summary: Tendo keeps the plan postponed. Musa replies, “Okay. Tell me when you want to talk.” He is hurt; she can hear it even in two words. She does
paragraphs: Tendo keeps the plan postponed. Musa replies, “Okay. Tell me when you want to talk.” He is hurt; she can hear it even in two words. She does not send a reassuring answer she cannot stand behind.
Two days later they meet and speak more carefully. The pause did not solve the question. It gave her a chance to arrive with an answer that was hers.

When they finally speak, Musa says the silence made him imagine the worst. Tendo says a rushed reassurance would have been less honest. They set a way to ask for time without disappearing, a small agreement they both can keep.

opening.title: The signature
opening.summary: Kato’s father has signed a subject form for a future Kato did not choose.
paragraphs: Kato’s father has signed the subject selection form and left it beside the breakfast plates. Physics, Chemistry, Mathematics. The deadline is this morning.

Kato is sixteen. He does well enough in science, which is why his father calls engineering “the sensible road.” Kato likes computing and art: making little game worlds on an old laptop, testing them on cousins who complain loudly about every level. His father has never seen one. Kato has also never shown him a timetable, a course, or a person paid to do that work.
At school, his teacher is collecting forms before the first bell. His father’s signature is already there. Kato’s pen is in his pocket.

choices.label: Submit the signed form and test the subjects for one term.
Change the form to include computing and art, then face the conversation.
Ask the teacher for a meeting before the form is final.

submit.title: The safe route
submit.summary: The teacher accepts the form. At lunch Kato learns that the art group has only one place left and computing clashes with Chemistry. A term-l
paragraphs: The teacher accepts the form. At lunch Kato learns that the art group has only one place left and computing clashes with Chemistry. A term-long trial may close both options.

His father messages, “Proud of you.” Kato knows the message is sincere. He can ask the teacher whether a trial with a review date is possible, or tell his father that he signed before the decision was really made.

The signed combination clashes with the computing club. A written review could keep a route back to art but not guarantee a place; telling his father tonight starts the argument before any trial marks exist.

choices.label: Ask for a written review after the first month.
Tell his father tonight what the form cost him.

change.title: The new form
change.summary: Kato crosses out Physics and Chemistry and replaces them with computing and art, keeping Mathematics. He leaves his father’s signature untou
paragraphs: Kato crosses out Physics and Chemistry and replaces them with computing and art, keeping Mathematics. He leaves his father’s signature untouched. The teacher points to the changed subject list: the signature approved the earlier combination, not this one. She asks for confirmation from home before submitting it.
Kato’s father is working across town and may not pick up before the deadline. Kato can call and explain now, or leave the form with the teacher and hope it goes through.

His father can answer for five minutes before a meeting. Kato has screenshots of the game he built, but has not checked course costs. Holding the form avoids a rushed call and risks losing the last art place.

choices.label: Call his father and make his case with examples of his work.
Ask the teacher to hold the altered form without telling him yet.

teacher.title: The meeting
teacher.summary: The teacher can reserve the last art place until the end of the day. She asks Kato what he has made and what else he has researched. He show
paragraphs: The teacher can reserve the last art place until the end of the day. She asks Kato what he has made and what else he has researched. He shows a small game, then admits he does not know which subjects he needs after school.
She offers to speak with his father, but the decision cannot be made by a teacher alone. Kato can invite him into the discussion, or use the day to gather facts before asking for a new deadline.
His father can attend today. Kato can bring the unfinished plan into that meeting, or use another day to check courses while the remaining places are allocated.

choices.label: Invite his father to a three-way meeting today.
Use the day to compare courses and request one more day.

submit_try.title: The term
submit_try.summary: The teacher agrees to a one-month review, but cannot hold the art place. Kato keeps Physics and Mathematics while attending an after-school
paragraphs: The teacher agrees to a one-month review, but cannot hold the art place. Kato keeps Physics and Mathematics while attending an after-school design club. His father says the club is fine as long as grades hold.
At the review Kato brings a finished project and his marks. He has evidence for a new discussion, though the subject he wanted most may have to wait another year.

Kato shows his father the design-club project at the review. His Physics mark has held; his interest in building games has not faded. They ask the teacher which change is still possible next term and put the answer beside the original form.

submit_talk.title: The kitchen
submit_talk.summary: His father listens while Kato explains the timetable clash. “Why did you submit it?” he asks. “Because you had signed it,” Kato says. Neithe
paragraphs: His father listens while Kato explains the timetable clash. “Why did you submit it?” he asks. “Because you had signed it,” Kato says. Neither enjoys that answer.

They meet the teacher the next morning. Art is full, but computing has a space if Kato adjusts another subject. They make a new plan that keeps Mathematics. It is less neat than the form on the table and more like a decision made by three people.

On the new timetable Kato still has difficult Mathematics homework. His father helps with a problem, then asks what the computing class made that week. Kato shows him a clumsy game level. His father loses immediately and requests a rematch.

change_tell.title: The explanation
change_tell.summary: Kato calls his father with screenshots of his game and a list of courses he found. His father asks sharp questions about fees and jobs; Kato
paragraphs: Kato calls his father with screenshots of his game and a list of courses he found. His father asks sharp questions about fees and jobs; Kato can answer some, not all. He agrees to come to school after lunch.
The teacher holds the art place. They settle on Mathematics, computing, and art, with a date to review results. Kato’s father asks to play the game that evening. He is terrible at level one.

His father writes down three questions about fees, training and jobs for their next discussion. Kato researches them instead of treating the first meeting as a final victory. The game remains on his father’s phone, where a cousin keeps beating his score.

change_hide.title: The call
change_hide.summary: The teacher holds the form but refuses to submit the changed subject list without fresh parental confirmation. The signature itself has not
paragraphs: The teacher holds the form but refuses to submit the changed subject list without fresh parental confirmation. The signature itself has not been altered. Kato spends the afternoon waiting for a call he has avoided making. The last art place goes to another student.

At home he tells his father about the subjects he changed after the form was signed. His father is upset that the old signature was presented as approval of a new choice. They begin the conversation late, with fewer options on the timetable.

Kato and his father visit the teacher together after the art place is gone. Computing is still possible. His father asks Kato to bring him into decisions before the deadline next time; Kato asks him not to sign first. They both agree, without pretending the lost place returns.

teacher_join.title: The timetable
teacher_join.summary: His father arrives carrying a work folder. Kato shows the game and the teacher shows the subject requirements. His father still worries abou
paragraphs: His father arrives carrying a work folder. Kato shows the game and the teacher shows the subject requirements. His father still worries about income; Kato still cannot promise an outcome.

They choose a combination that keeps Mathematics and computing, and Kato joins art as an extra subject if the timetable allows. His father calls it an experiment. Kato calls it his first honest application.

At home the father tells an uncle that Kato is studying computing and art. Kato corrects him: art is an extra subject for now. His father accepts the correction in front of the uncle, which is more useful to Kato than praise given privately.

teacher_wait.title: The deadline
teacher_wait.summary: Kato spends the afternoon speaking to two older students and checking course requirements. The teacher secures a one-day extension, but not
paragraphs: Kato spends the afternoon speaking to two older students and checking course requirements. The teacher secures a one-day extension, but not the art place. He goes home with a clearer case and a real deadline.

His father is surprised by how much work Kato has done. They agree to computing and Mathematics, then plan an art portfolio outside the timetable. It is a compromise Kato can name, including what he gave up.

Kato starts a portfolio in a folder named for the date of the extension. The first pieces are uneven. At the next school meeting he shows the work and the course requirements together, because he no longer wants his case to depend on a single impressive drawing.

opening.title: The interview
opening.summary: Sarah brought her certificate to an interview. The “job” pays nothing.
paragraphs: Sarah reaches the office in Kampala with her certificate in a plastic folder and UGX 12,000 left for transport. The interviewer offers her a “trial”: five days of work, no pay, no guarantee of a job. She needs two taxis each day.

Sarah is nineteen and finished school three months ago. At home she said today was her first day at work. Her family has started planning what she might contribute to the electricity bill. The receptionist quietly tells her that three other applicants did the same trial last month.

The interviewer is waiting for her answer. Outside, her aunt has texted asking whether she can help at the market this week for a small daily wage. Neither option resembles the independence Sarah imagined at graduation.
Uncle Rwamiti is coordinating the market shift her aunt offered as a fallback.

choices.label: Ask the interviewer for clear terms and what happened to past trainees.
Take the trial for one day and see what the work is.
Leave and tell her family the offer is unpaid.

terms.title: The trial
terms.summary: The interviewer says the trial teaches valuable skills, but cannot say how many people are hired or cover transport. The receptionist later
paragraphs: The interviewer says the trial teaches valuable skills, but cannot say how many people are hired or cover transport. The receptionist later says one trainee was offered a role; two were not.

Sarah can negotiate one paid assessment day with written expectations, or decline and use the afternoon to apply elsewhere. Her certificate is still in her hand; so is the cost of another return trip.

Outside the office, Sarah counts the fare left in her wallet. Uncle Rwamiti calls about the market shift her aunt offered. It pays tomorrow, but taking it means admitting that today’s interview was never a job offer. Asking the office for different terms risks losing even the trial. Keeping the afternoon free means going home with applications instead of an answer everyone can celebrate.

choices.label: Ask for a paid one-day assessment and written terms.
Decline and spend her fare on targeted applications nearby.

take.title: The first day
take.summary: The first day is mostly photocopying and entering numbers into a spreadsheet. Sarah learns the system quickly. At five, the supervisor asks
paragraphs: The first day is mostly photocopying and entering numbers into a spreadsheet. Sarah learns the system quickly. At five, the supervisor asks her to come back tomorrow and bring her own laptop.
Sarah’s transport money will cover one more day, not four. She can ask for fare support and a defined task, or pretend the trial is already a job while she borrows money to continue.

At the taxi stage, Uncle Rwamiti asks whether her first day paid for the ride home. Sarah nearly says the salary comes later. He is checking who will cover her aunt’s market shift tomorrow and needs an answer, not a success story. Returning to the office may produce useful experience. It will also use another day and fare that belong to a real alternative.

choices.label: Ask for transport support and a clear evaluation before returning.
Borrow fare from home and finish the week without raising the issue.

leave.title: The walk
leave.summary: Sarah tells her mother on the phone that there is no salary. Her mother is disappointed, then asks what the office actually offered. Sarah r
paragraphs: Sarah tells her mother on the phone that there is no salary. Her mother is disappointed, then asks what the office actually offered. Sarah realises she only asked whether they wanted her, not what she would learn.
Her aunt’s market shift starts tomorrow. Sarah can take it while making a job-search plan, or go home today to research paid openings and training routes with her family.

Uncle Rwamiti says her aunt needs someone to record sales as well as move stock. Sarah had pictured carrying sacks while friends began office jobs. The work might give her both wages and figures she can show another employer. Going home would give her a quiet afternoon to research. Neither option is the independence she announced at breakfast; both could make tomorrow more specific.

choices.label: Take the market shift and set aside time each day for applications.
Go home and build a specific four-week search plan.

terms_day.title: The contract
terms_day.summary: The interviewer refuses a paid day but offers to send written tasks. Sarah declines the week. She spends UGX 2,000 printing two tailored app
paragraphs: The interviewer refuses a paid day but offers to send written tasks. Sarah declines the week. She spends UGX 2,000 printing two tailored applications and keeps enough for the ride home.
One employer calls the following week; it is only another interview. Sarah goes knowing the pay range and transport route. Those details make the opportunity less magical and more possible to judge.

Sarah keeps a record of the questions she asked about pay and transport. At the next interview she asks them before agreeing to a trial. The recruiter answers plainly; she can weigh an actual offer instead of guessing what “opportunity” will cost her.

terms_exit.title: The search
terms_exit.summary: Sarah leaves with the afternoon free. She visits two nearby offices that actually advertise paid entry roles, learns one requires a skill sh
paragraphs: Sarah leaves with the afternoon free. She visits two nearby offices that actually advertise paid entry roles, learns one requires a skill she lacks, and writes it down.
At home she explains the trial and the new leads. Her mother is not delighted, but she stops calling the unpaid office “the job.” Sarah’s folder now holds a list beside the certificate.

The missing skill turns out to be a spreadsheet function she can learn at the community centre. Sarah registers for an evening session and continues applying for paid work. Her certificate is still useful, but now it has a specific next skill beside it.

take_ask.title: The ledger
take_ask.summary: The supervisor says there is no transport allowance. Sarah asks for a written evaluation and one useful project. She receives a spreadsheet
paragraphs: The supervisor says there is no transport allowance. Sarah asks for a written evaluation and one useful project. She receives a spreadsheet task she can finish that day and adds it to her portfolio with permission.
She does not return for the unpaid week. She has spent one fare to learn something real and can describe that skill in the next interview.

She writes the project on her CV without calling the unpaid day a job. When an interviewer asks what she actually did, she can explain the spreadsheet and the terms she negotiated. It is a better answer than the title the office would have given her.

take_hide.title: The fare
take_hide.summary: Sarah borrows fare from her brother. Each evening she says work went well. On Friday the office thanks her but has no opening. Her brother a
paragraphs: Sarah borrows fare from her brother. Each evening she says work went well. On Friday the office thanks her but has no opening. Her brother asks when she can repay him.

Sarah shows him the message and tells him the terms she had hidden. He helps her list what she did learn, then reminds her that a certificate and a week of unpaid work do not become wages by being called a job.

Her brother agrees to let her repay the fare in small amounts. Sarah asks the office for a written record of her tasks, then uses it to describe her experience accurately. At home she starts saying “interview” and “trial” when that is what they are.

leave_home.title: The plan
leave_home.summary: Sarah and her mother make a four-week plan: three applications a week, a short computer course at the community centre, and a date to review
paragraphs: Sarah and her mother make a four-week plan: three applications a week, a short computer course at the community centre, and a date to review what gets replies. Her mother asks her to help with the electricity bill when paid work begins, not before.
The plan does not deliver a job by supper. It does make Tuesday different from Monday. Sarah sets an alarm for the course registration and puts her certificate where she can find it.

In week two, two applications receive no reply and one leads to a test. Sarah adjusts the plan rather than hiding the silence from her family. Her mother asks what the test involves, then helps her find a quiet place to prepare.

leave_market.title: The stall
leave_market.summary: Her aunt pays her to help sort stock. Sarah learns which suppliers change prices without warning and is trusted to keep a simple sales recor
paragraphs: Her aunt pays her to help sort stock. Sarah learns which suppliers change prices without warning and is trusted to keep a simple sales record. She uses the afternoons for applications.

A friend jokes that a graduate is back at a market stall. Sarah dislikes the joke, then counts the day’s earnings. It is temporary work, and real work. She can decide what comes next with fare in her pocket.

A month later Sarah applies for a paid stock-control role using the sales record she built at the stall. Her aunt insists she list the market work by name. The interview is not a promise, but Sarah arrives with figures she produced herself.

opening.title: It Was Only a Joke
opening.summary: The mattress is a joke. The packed bag is not.
paragraphs: Isaac catches the mattress as it slides through the dormitory window. His friends are laughing. Inside, fourteen-year-old Musa stands beside an empty bed, holding the sheet they have tied into a football. It is Saturday visiting day at their school in Wakiso.

Isaac is sixteen. He laughs once before he sees Musa packing his clothes into a supermarket bag. “My uncle is at the gate,” Musa says. “I am going.” Brian, Isaac’s closest friend, whispers, “Bring the mattress back quietly. You will spoil the whole joke.”
The dorm prefect is crossing the compound. Musa has stopped packing long enough to look at Isaac.
Uncle Rwamiti is here to visit Isaac’s cousin, with a flask that leaks.

choices.label: Tell the group to stop and return Musa’s things.
Return Musa’s things and ask him privately what he needs.
Bring the dorm prefect over before things go further.

challenge.title: The audience
challenge.summary: Isaac puts the mattress down and tells the group to return the sheet. The laughter stops, then Brian laughs louder. “Now you are headmaster?
paragraphs: Isaac puts the mattress down and tells the group to return the sheet. The laughter stops, then Brian laughs louder. “Now you are headmaster?” Two boys return Musa’s shoes. Someone else starts recording Isaac.

Musa says this is the third time. Brian arranged the previous two as well. Isaac had thought Brian was simply watching. Musa asks him not to make a speech with his name in it; he wants his things back and somewhere he can sleep.

Uncle Rwamiti, visiting Isaac’s cousin, appears carrying a flask. He sets it on the windowsill and helps lift the mattress inside. “This bed has an address,” he says. Brian asks Isaac to tell the prefect it was just play. The prefect is close enough to hear the next answer.

choices.label: Describe what happened to the prefect, with Musa beside you if he wants.
Ask Brian to return everything and speak to Musa privately.

help.title: The missing shoe
help.summary: Isaac carries the mattress back without challenging the group. Musa lets him straighten the sheet, but keeps packing. One shoe is missing. I
paragraphs: Isaac carries the mattress back without challenging the group. Musa lets him straighten the sheet, but keeps packing. One shoe is missing. Isaac offers to find it; Musa says Brian hid it and knows exactly where it is.

This was not the first prank. Musa shows Isaac a message saying the group will hide his bag next week. Brian has sent it from his own number. Musa asks Isaac not to forward it around. “Everyone already knows my bed,” he says.

Uncle Rwamiti arrives with a visiting flask and searches under the beds alongside Isaac. He finds two ancient biscuits but no shoe. Musa’s uncle phones from the gate. Brian offers to return the shoe if Musa stays quiet. Musa asks Isaac to wait with him while he decides whether to leave.

choices.label: Walk with Musa to his uncle and explain what you witnessed.
Ask the prefect for a different bed and a private check-in tonight.

prefect.title: Who started it
prefect.summary: Isaac calls the prefect. The boys scatter before the mattress is back inside. Brian stays and says the whole dorm was involved. Musa points
paragraphs: Isaac calls the prefect. The boys scatter before the mattress is back inside. Brian stays and says the whole dorm was involved. Musa points at Brian: “He planned it.” Isaac realises that the friend who asked for quiet was also the organiser.

The prefect wants names before the duty teacher arrives. Musa asks whether he will be made to repeat everything in front of the dorm. Isaac saw the mattress being passed, but did not see who first took it. Naming everyone would be easier than explaining that gap.
