Uncle Rwamiti helps carry the mattress back. He asks Musa where he wants it placed instead of deciding for him. The prefect hands Isaac a sheet of paper. Brian mouths, “You laughed too.” That part is true.

choices.label: Give your own account, including your laughter and what you did not see.
Ask for a private meeting with Musa before names are announced.

challenge--record.title: The written account
challenge--record.summary: Isaac refuses Brian’s request to call it play. He asks Musa whether he wants to speak or have Isaac describe what he saw. Musa lets Isaac be
paragraphs: Isaac refuses Brian’s request to call it play. He asks Musa whether he wants to speak or have Isaac describe what he saw. Musa lets Isaac begin, then adds the two earlier incidents. Isaac admits that he laughed before he intervened.

The prefect writes their separate accounts and brings the duty teacher. Musa calls his uncle; he decides to stay tonight after the teacher arranges another bed and a check-in. That does not settle Brian’s anger. He ignores Isaac at supper, and the recording still needs reporting.

On Monday, Musa asks Isaac to help collect a missing exercise book. He does not thank him in front of everybody. Brian leaves a space at their usual table. Isaac sits there anyway, uncertain whether the space is an invitation or a warning.

challenge--private.title: The private repair
challenge--private.summary: After stopping the group publicly, Isaac takes Brian aside. He asks him to return the sheet and delete his own recording. Brian does both, t
paragraphs: After stopping the group publicly, Isaac takes Brian aside. He asks him to return the sheet and delete his own recording. Brian does both, then says Musa can apologise for being dramatic. Isaac brings him to the doorway without promising an apology.

Musa will not speak alone with Brian. Isaac stays while Brian admits arranging the mattress stunt, but Brian avoids mentioning the earlier incidents. Musa calls his uncle and leaves for the weekend. A returned mattress has not made tonight feel safe.

The prefect sees the empty bed and asks Isaac what happened. The quiet agreement has lasted less than an hour. Isaac now has to decide how much of the conversation to recount, while Brian stands behind him waiting for their friendship to do the talking.

help--escort.title: At the gate
help--escort.summary: Isaac keeps the message off the dormitory group and walks Musa to the gate. With Musa’s permission, he tells the uncle about the mattress an
paragraphs: Isaac keeps the message off the dormitory group and walks Musa to the gate. With Musa’s permission, he tells the uncle about the mattress and missing shoe. Musa shows the message himself. His uncle asks for the duty teacher before taking him away.

The shoe turns up when the teacher calls Brian out. Musa still goes home for the weekend. The teacher agrees to speak with him before he returns, rather than announce a resolution to the dormitory. Isaac has helped him leave safely; he has not persuaded him to stay.

Brian sends Isaac a voice note about betrayal. Isaac listens while carrying the now empty supermarket bag back to the dorm. On Sunday Musa texts: “Keep my maths book somewhere.” It is a small request, and a much more useful one than asking him to feel better.

help--stay.title: A different bed
help--stay.summary: Isaac asks Musa before approaching the prefect. Musa agrees to a different bed if nobody announces why. The prefect finds a space near his o
paragraphs: Isaac asks Musa before approaching the prefect. Musa agrees to a different bed if nobody announces why. The prefect finds a space near his own and brings the duty teacher into the arrangement. Isaac tells them about the threat, with Musa choosing who sees the message.

Musa phones his uncle and decides to try one night. Brian returns the shoe without the silence he wanted in exchange. He calls Isaac a prefect’s assistant. Isaac replies that assistants should at least receive a badge; nobody laughs much.

At lights-out the prefect checks on Musa. He is still awake. Isaac cannot promise there will be no retaliation, but tomorrow’s check-in has a person and a time. Musa puts his bag beneath the new bed instead of unpacking it completely.

prefect--limits.title: Names with limits
prefect--limits.summary: Having brought the prefect, Isaac writes what he actually witnessed. He includes his own laugh, Brian’s request for silence and Musa’s state
paragraphs: Having brought the prefect, Isaac writes what he actually witnessed. He includes his own laugh, Brian’s request for silence and Musa’s statement about the planning. He leaves the beginning of the incident marked as something he did not see.

The duty teacher asks Musa for a separate conversation. Musa chooses to have his uncle there. Brian cannot turn Isaac’s laughter into proof that Musa enjoyed it, but Isaac is questioned about it all the same. The inquiry takes the rest of visiting afternoon.

Musa gets his belongings and leaves with his uncle for the weekend. Isaac’s cousin complains that they missed their visit. Uncle Rwamiti pours the cold tea anyway. Nobody can give that afternoon back, and nobody has to invent an account to explain where it went.

prefect--privacy.title: Behind the office door
prefect--privacy.summary: Isaac asks the prefect to move the conversation out of the dormitory. Musa agrees. Brian objects that Isaac has already called authority int
paragraphs: Isaac asks the prefect to move the conversation out of the dormitory. Musa agrees. Brian objects that Isaac has already called authority into it; he wants to defend himself in front of everyone. The prefect tells him he will get his own turn.

In the office, Musa describes the earlier incidents. Isaac only confirms the things he witnessed today. The teacher contacts Musa’s uncle and arranges a different bed pending follow-up. Musa decides to remain, with the option to call home again tonight.

Back in the dormitory, the boys ask what Musa said. Isaac refuses to recite it. That earns him a new nickname by supper. Musa sits beside the prefect, not Isaac. The private meeting has protected a conversation, while leaving Isaac to manage a very public friendship problem.

opening.title: The Paper Before the Paper
opening.summary: Tomorrow’s exam is allegedly on WhatsApp. Your number is in the screenshot.
paragraphs: Shamim’s phone lights up beside her revision notes. In a Mukono WhatsApp group, someone posts photographs headed “Tomorrow’s paper”. A price follows: UGX 15,000. Her best friend Ruth messages, “I paid. Don’t tell me I wasted it.”

Shamim is seventeen. She joined for revision questions, and has not paid or asked for a paper. The administrator says anyone doubting the pictures can leave. The first photograph resembles a practice question their teacher used last term.
Ruth asks whether Shamim will study the photos with her tonight. In the group, someone starts a poll: who is ready?
At her aunt’s home, Uncle Rwamiti has brought back their repaired kettle.

choices.label: Leave the group and revise from your own notes.
Ask the seller where the pictures came from before trusting them.
Ask a trusted teacher to check the claim privately.

leave.title: Your number remains
leave.summary: Shamim leaves without downloading the remaining photographs. She tells Ruth she will use her notes. Ten minutes later another classmate send
paragraphs: Shamim leaves without downloading the remaining photographs. She tells Ruth she will use her notes. Ten minutes later another classmate sends a screenshot of the group membership: Shamim’s number is circled under “people with the paper”. Leaving has not removed the earlier membership list.

Ruth says that screenshot proves nothing. She also says the seller has blocked her after payment. Shamim has her own messages showing why she joined, but cannot prove what every other member received.

Uncle Rwamiti, delivering a repaired kettle to her aunt, hears her phone buzz again. “That kettle has fewer groups than your phone, and still refuses to work.” He leaves it on the table. A class representative asks Shamim whether the screenshot is genuine.

choices.label: Give the class representative your own timeline and ask them to correct the claim.
Ask a trusted teacher to review the screenshot privately.

question.title: A screenshot for sale
question.summary: Shamim asks how the seller knows these are tomorrow’s questions. Instead of evidence, he posts her question with the caption “Interested buy
paragraphs: Shamim asks how the seller knows these are tomorrow’s questions. Instead of evidence, he posts her question with the caption “Interested buyer”. Ruth tells him to remove it; he demands another payment to do that. Neither girl sends more money.

Shamim’s question was a challenge, but cropped out of the conversation it looks like a purchase enquiry. Ruth’s paid pictures include a page from last term’s practice sheet. That weakens the seller’s claim without proving what every page is.

Uncle Rwamiti is fixing the kettle plug nearby. He glances at the caption Shamim shows him. “Even my broken kettle has become an interested buyer. I asked its price.” The seller gives Shamim five minutes to pay for removal; classmates begin forwarding his post.

choices.label: Share the surrounding messages to correct the cropped claim.
Take the threats and original exchange to a trusted teacher.

check.title: Receipt is not proof
check.summary: Shamim shows a trusted teacher the post without forwarding it into another group. The teacher says a familiar question cannot establish that
paragraphs: Shamim shows a trusted teacher the post without forwarding it into another group. The teacher says a familiar question cannot establish that a whole paper is genuine and starts the school’s reporting process. Shamim is asked to keep her original messages.

Ruth then receives a membership screenshot with both girls’ numbers circled. The teacher has not sent it; it came from the seller’s group. Ruth fears Shamim accused her of cheating. Shamim had reported a claim, not witnessed Ruth use any material in an exam.

Uncle Rwamiti, visiting with a repaired kettle, hears Ruth’s upset call through the speaker. He quietly switches it off speaker and hands Shamim the phone. The teacher offers a meeting after revision. Ruth says she will only attend if Shamim explains exactly what she reported.

choices.label: Tell Ruth exactly what you reported and offer to attend the meeting together.
Give the teacher your own account and leave Ruth to decide whether to speak.

leave--explain.title: A corrected caption
leave--explain.summary: Shamim says the membership screenshot is genuine, but the claim that she bought a paper is not. She shows when she joined and left, keeping
paragraphs: Shamim says the membership screenshot is genuine, but the claim that she bought a paper is not. She shows when she joined and left, keeping Ruth’s payment conversation private. The representative changes the caption and asks people to stop circulating numbers.

Two classmates have already forwarded the original. Shamim spends part of her revision evening sending the correction to them. Ruth still has no refund and asks for ordinary notes. Shamim shares those, but does not open the alleged paper.

The exam contains a familiar topic, which is enough for someone to revive the rumour afterwards. Shamim has a clear account of her own actions, not a guarantee that everyone will believe it. She saves the correction with her messages instead of starting another argument in the group.

leave--teacher.title: The private record
leave--teacher.summary: After leaving the group, Shamim takes the membership screenshot and her own messages to a trusted teacher. She distinguishes what she saw fr
paragraphs: After leaving the group, Shamim takes the membership screenshot and her own messages to a trusted teacher. She distinguishes what she saw from what she heard. The teacher records that membership alone does not show purchase and asks her not to circulate the alleged paper.

The teacher follows the school’s reporting process and cannot promise complete secrecy. Shamim tells Ruth she has asked for help with the accusation about her number. Ruth feels exposed even though Shamim did not offer her private payment messages.

The seller remains unreachable. Shamim sits the exam from her revision notes and leaves the outcome of the report to the adults handling it. At lunch Ruth sits elsewhere. Later she asks what the teacher actually said. It is the first conversation that day without a forwarded screenshot in it.

question--context.title: The missing lines
question--context.summary: Having challenged the seller, Shamim shares her question with the surrounding messages. She covers classmates’ numbers and Ruth’s private pa
paragraphs: Having challenged the seller, Shamim shares her question with the surrounding messages. She covers classmates’ numbers and Ruth’s private payment details. The demand for money to remove the post is visible. The representative puts her correction beside the cropped screenshot.

The seller deletes his own post, but copies remain. Shamim blocks him and saves the exchange. Ruth wants to warn other buyers; Shamim helps her describe the blocked payment without claiming they have verified an actual exam leak.

They revise together using their old practice sheet. Ruth is angry about the lost UGX 15,000 and worried about who saw her name. When a new account offers “confirmed questions”, neither girl answers. Tomorrow still requires an exam, and their evening has become shorter than they planned.

question--report.title: The original exchange
question--report.summary: Shamim sends no removal fee. She takes the seller’s threat, her original question and the cropped version to a trusted teacher. She explains
paragraphs: Shamim sends no removal fee. She takes the seller’s threat, her original question and the cropped version to a trusted teacher. She explains that she questioned the source and has not verified that the pictures are an exam paper.

The teacher preserves the evidence and uses the school’s reporting process. Shamim blocks the seller after saving the exchange. Ruth asks whether she will be punished for paying. Shamim cannot answer for the teacher, and offers to accompany her to ask directly.

Ruth agrees, reluctantly. They spend revision time explaining separate actions instead of pretending they did the same thing. The money may not return. On exam morning, Shamim leaves her phone at home; the problem it recorded has not disappeared, but it no longer gets to interrupt every line she reads.

check--together.title: Two separate accounts
check--together.summary: Shamim tells Ruth she asked a teacher to verify the seller’s claim and showed the public post. She did not say she saw Ruth cheat. Ruth stil
paragraphs: Shamim tells Ruth she asked a teacher to verify the seller’s claim and showed the public post. She did not say she saw Ruth cheat. Ruth still dislikes the report, but agrees to attend the meeting with her own payment messages.

The teacher separates group membership, buying alleged material and any actual examination conduct. The girls do not get a promise about the investigation’s result. Ruth gets advice on preserving the payment record instead of sending a second fee to the seller.

They return to revision later than intended. Ruth asks for ten quiet minutes before discussing it again. Shamim gives them to her. Their friendship has not returned to normal; it has acquired an accurate version of what each person did, which is somewhere to begin.

check--own.title: A boundary on the record
check--own.summary: Having asked for the private check, Shamim submits only her own account: how she joined, what appeared and what she reported. She tells Ruth
paragraphs: Having asked for the private check, Shamim submits only her own account: how she joined, what appeared and what she reported. She tells Ruth about the meeting but does not speak for her or provide the private payment conversation.

Ruth declines to attend that evening. The teacher warns that further questions may follow through the school’s process. Shamim saves her messages and stops trying to promise Ruth an outcome she cannot control. Ruth takes her revision books to another friend’s house.

After the exam, they compare a normal question from their notes. They do not compare the seller’s photographs. Ruth has not recovered her money and Shamim has not recovered their easy conversation. Both remain possible future tasks, separate from proving something the girls never verified.

opening.title: Lend Me Your Sweater
opening.summary: Your friend needs a sweater. The debate organiser needs her on stage.
paragraphs: “Give me your sweater. Quickly.” Akello turns to find her friend Lamwaka pulling her skirt behind her. There is a period stain. Outside the washroom at their Gulu neighbourhood debate event, the organiser calls Lamwaka’s name into a microphone.

Akello is fifteen. Lamwaka has prepared for this debate for weeks. The nearest shop has supplies, but Akello only has their transport money. A replacement speaker waits by the door, impatient. Lamwaka says, “Please don’t tell everyone.”
Akello ties the sweater round her friend’s waist. The organiser calls again.
Uncle Rwamiti is helping run the event timetable and the unreliable microphone.

choices.label: Quietly find supplies while Lamwaka waits in the washroom.
Ask the organiser for a short delay without explaining Lamwaka’s situation.
Offer to accompany Lamwaka home if she wants to leave.

supplies.title: The replacement speaks
supplies.summary: Akello asks the woman running the refreshments stall for help without naming Lamwaka. She has a sealed pad and lends it to her. Akello keeps
paragraphs: Akello asks the woman running the refreshments stall for help without naming Lamwaka. She has a sealed pad and lends it to her. Akello keeps their transport money. When she returns, the replacement speaker is already onstage.
He says Lamwaka has “girl problems” and people near the front laugh. Lamwaka hears him through the window. She now has supplies, but does not want to walk back into that room as an announcement.

Uncle Rwamiti is arguing with a microphone that whistles whenever he approaches it. He sees Akello at the doorway and asks whether Lamwaka wants a pause or another slot. He does not ask for the reason. Lamwaka says she wants the remark stopped, but has not decided whether she wants to speak.

choices.label: Ask the organiser to stop the remarks and let Lamwaka choose her slot.
Stay with Lamwaka and help her leave if that is what she wants.

delay.title: An unwanted introduction
delay.summary: Akello asks for ten minutes, saying Lamwaka needs a private pause. The organiser agrees and puts the replacement speaker first. The replacem
paragraphs: Akello asks for ten minutes, saying Lamwaka needs a private pause. The organiser agrees and puts the replacement speaker first. The replacement overhears a washroom conversation and tells the room he is standing in because Lamwaka has “girl problems”.
Lamwaka grips the borrowed sweater. The delay has protected time, but not privacy. Akello has not yet found supplies; a stallholder offers to help if Lamwaka wants her to come to the washroom.

Uncle Rwamiti, holding the event timetable upside down, asks which name should move. Akello says Lamwaka must choose. He turns the timetable around. “Good. This paper has been choosing for everybody all morning.” The organiser asks whether Lamwaka will return after the break.

choices.label: Ask Lamwaka if she wants supplies and a later slot, then pass on her answer.
Support Lamwaka’s request to withdraw and ask the organiser to stop the comment.

home.title: News travels ahead
home.summary: Lamwaka accepts Akello’s offer. They tell the organiser she is withdrawing and head for the taxi stage with the sweater tied round her waist
paragraphs: Lamwaka accepts Akello’s offer. They tell the organiser she is withdrawing and head for the taxi stage with the sweater tied round her waist. On the way, a friend calls: the replacement speaker has announced “girl problems” to the hall.

Lamwaka stops walking. She had chosen a quiet exit, not a public explanation. She wants to send an angry message to the event group; it would reveal the very detail she asked Akello to keep private. Their taxi is filling.

Uncle Rwamiti, fetching another chair from outside, catches up to give them Lamwaka’s notebook. He asks whether she wants him to deliver any message. Lamwaka says, “Not a speech.” He nods. “My speeches cost extra anyway.” She must decide what to ask him to say.

choices.label: Help Lamwaka request a correction that does not explain her body.
Continue home and let Lamwaka decide later whether to contact the organiser.

supplies--organiser.title: A slot without an explanation
supplies--organiser.summary: After finding supplies, Akello tells the organiser that the replacement made a personal remark which needs stopping. She does not explain La
paragraphs: After finding supplies, Akello tells the organiser that the replacement made a personal remark which needs stopping. She does not explain Lamwaka’s stain. The organiser corrects him privately and tells the room to keep introductions about the debate.

Lamwaka chooses a later slot. She keeps the sweater around her waist and asks Akello to sit near the aisle. Her opening line comes out shakily; the second is louder. She finishes without discussing why she was delayed.

They miss the first taxi they planned to take. At the stage, Lamwaka complains about the replacement’s argument as fiercely as ever, then asks whether anyone laughed when she returned. Akello answers honestly. The debate is over; the embarrassment is taking a little longer.

supplies--leave.title: The walk outside
supplies--leave.summary: Akello offers to stay outside with Lamwaka rather than negotiate a return to the stage. Lamwaka chooses to go home. Akello tells the organis
paragraphs: Akello offers to stay outside with Lamwaka rather than negotiate a return to the stage. Lamwaka chooses to go home. Akello tells the organiser they are leaving and asks him to stop the personal remarks, without giving a medical explanation.

They use the transport money Akello kept when she borrowed supplies. Lamwaka is upset about losing her chance to speak. Akello lets her complain without saying she ought to have been brave. At home, Lamwaka asks for the debate results anyway.

The organiser later offers a place at the next event and says he has addressed the remark. Lamwaka does not accept immediately. Akello’s sweater comes back washed two days later, folded around a note: “Next time, sit in the front. I may need a hostile audience for practice.”

delay--return.title: Her own answer
delay--return.summary: Having requested the delay, Akello asks Lamwaka what she wants before answering the organiser. Lamwaka accepts the stallholder’s help and a
paragraphs: Having requested the delay, Akello asks Lamwaka what she wants before answering the organiser. Lamwaka accepts the stallholder’s help and a later slot. She asks that the replacement stop introducing her. Akello passes on both requests without the private details.

The organiser apologises to Lamwaka and changes the running order. She returns with the sweater still tied on, gives her speech and declines a photograph afterwards. Akello also declines when somebody tries to include them both.

On their way home Lamwaka says she is pleased she spoke and angry that everyone had an opinion about her body first. Akello can hold both complaints at once. The next event’s invitation goes directly to Lamwaka, so her reply will not need a messenger.

delay--withdraw.title: The empty speaking slot
delay--withdraw.summary: Akello tells the organiser that Lamwaka has chosen to withdraw. She asks him to stop the replacement’s personal comments, without explaining
paragraphs: Akello tells the organiser that Lamwaka has chosen to withdraw. She asks him to stop the replacement’s personal comments, without explaining the stain. The stallholder gives Lamwaka supplies before they leave.

The organiser apologises, but Lamwaka does not change her mind. At the taxi stage she asks Akello whether requesting the delay made everything worse. Akello explains exactly what she said and what the replacement added on his own.

Lamwaka saves her speech instead of deleting it. They rehearse the funniest paragraph on the ride home, quietly enough not to become a second event. The stage opportunity has gone today; the words she prepared still belong to her.

home--message.title: A message on her terms
home--message.summary: After choosing to accompany Lamwaka home, Akello helps her write: “Please stop discussing why I withdrew. I did not consent to that introduc
paragraphs: After choosing to accompany Lamwaka home, Akello helps her write: “Please stop discussing why I withdrew. I did not consent to that introduction.” Lamwaka approves it and asks Uncle Rwamiti to deliver it to the organiser.

They take the taxi. The organiser sends an apology and tells the event group to stop speculating. It cannot erase what was said, but Lamwaka does not have to add a full explanation to obtain a correction. Akello sits beside her while she switches off notifications.

At home Lamwaka reads her speech aloud once, for an audience of one and a saucepan. She still wishes she had competed. She also says she is glad she left when she wanted. Akello hands back the notebook, with its stage pages intact.

home--wait.title: After the noise
home--wait.summary: Akello tells Uncle Rwamiti that Lamwaka does not want a message delivered yet. She accompanies her home as offered. Lamwaka switches off her
paragraphs: Akello tells Uncle Rwamiti that Lamwaka does not want a message delivered yet. She accompanies her home as offered. Lamwaka switches off her phone; Akello sends no explanation to the event group on her behalf.

The rumours continue for a while without them. In the evening Lamwaka chooses to contact the organiser herself and asks why the replacement was allowed to discuss her. Akello sits nearby, available to help but not typing the answer.

The organiser offers an apology and another speaking slot. Lamwaka asks for time to consider it. Today’s withdrawal remains a missed chance, and tomorrow’s reply remains hers. Akello borrows a different sweater for the ride home because the first one is still doing its job.

opening.title: Your Passport, Today
opening.summary: The recruiter wants a passport by five. Your aunt has already borrowed the fee.
paragraphs: Denis is nineteen, standing outside a recruitment office in Nansana with his passport inside a brown envelope. A message says the overseas hotel job closes at five. His aunt borrowed UGX 300,000 for the processing fee this morning.

He wants this job. Months of applications have produced mostly silence. The man at reception says the passport must stay with them to secure the place. The message named a hotel, but the form on the desk says “general domestic placement”.
His aunt calls: “Have they accepted you?” Reception slides a pen towards him.
Uncle Rwamiti gave Denis a lift and is waiting outside with the boda.

choices.label: Ask for the employer, job terms and recruitment details in writing.
Ask an experienced person to join you at the office before proceeding.
Keep your passport and ask for time to consult before paying.

verify.title: A different job
verify.summary: Denis keeps the passport while asking for the promised hotel’s details and written terms. Reception prints a form with a different employer
paragraphs: Denis keeps the passport while asking for the promised hotel’s details and written terms. Reception prints a form with a different employer and a lower wage. The name of the agency on it also differs from the name on the advert. They say these are routine changes.

His aunt asks him not to lose the opportunity through too many questions. She has to begin repaying her loan next week. Denis now has documents to compare, but no confirmation that either version is legitimate.

Uncle Rwamiti, who gave Denis a lift, comes inside carrying the helmet he forgot to leave on the boda. He asks for a chair while Denis reads. “They have given you a pen. At least give your eyes a turn.” Reception says the deadline will not move.

choices.label: Keep your documents and verify the conflicting details before committing.
Request corrected written terms and show your aunt both versions before deciding.

company.title: A witness at the desk
company.summary: Denis phones a neighbour who has worked abroad and waits with his passport. When she arrives, she asks to read the contract. Reception produ
paragraphs: Denis phones a neighbour who has worked abroad and waits with his passport. When she arrives, she asks to read the contract. Reception produces one naming domestic work rather than the hotel job, with deductions the advert never mentioned.

The neighbour does not declare the job genuine or fraudulent. She points to the differences and asks how Denis can verify them independently. Reception says he should trust their experience. His aunt calls again, worried that the queue will cost him the place.

Uncle Rwamiti comes in from the boda with Denis’s forgotten water bottle. He puts it beside the contract. “First drink. Even paperwork can make you sweat.” The neighbour offers to accompany Denis to an independent verification contact, but that will take them past five.

choices.label: Leave together with the copies and verify before handing over anything.
Ask the neighbour to explain the changed terms to your aunt with you present.

delay.title: Time is called hesitation
delay.summary: Denis puts the passport envelope back in his bag and asks to return after consulting someone. Reception says hesitation will lose him the ho
paragraphs: Denis puts the passport envelope back in his bag and asks to return after consulting someone. Reception says hesitation will lose him the hotel place. Then a second staff member hands him a form describing domestic work. The two accounts do not match.

His aunt sends a voice note saying the lender has confirmed the first repayment date. She is not demanding that he take any job, but she sounds as though the money has already crossed the ocean and begun earning.

Uncle Rwamiti waits outside with a boda helmet and a bag of tomatoes. Denis shows him the two descriptions. He moves the tomatoes so Denis can sit. “These at least have agreed to be tomatoes.” Denis needs to decide what explanation to send his aunt before the office closes.

choices.label: Show your aunt the conflicting documents and ask to pause the application.
Ask for an extension and a matching written contract before any commitment.

verify--hold.title: The deadline passes
verify--hold.summary: Having requested the terms, Denis takes copies and keeps his passport. He tells reception he will verify the changed employer and agency thr
paragraphs: Having requested the terms, Denis takes copies and keeps his passport. He tells reception he will verify the changed employer and agency through independent official channels before signing or paying. They refuse to hold the place.

Five o’clock passes. Denis tells his aunt exactly which details differ and shows the forms. She is frightened about the loan and angry that the advert looked so definite. They arrange the first repayment from money Denis had saved for transport; it hurts before any job has been found.

He has no overseas placement tonight and no guarantee of another soon. He does have his passport and a record to check. Uncle Rwamiti drops him at home. The envelope comes back with him, flatter than when it left, but still closed around his own documents.

verify--clarify.title: Two forms at supper
verify--clarify.summary: Denis asks for a corrected offer rather than signing the contradictory form. Reception sends another document, but it changes only the headi
paragraphs: Denis asks for a corrected offer rather than signing the contradictory form. Reception sends another document, but it changes only the heading; the employer and pay still differ. He takes the copies home with his passport and does not pay the fee.

He shows his aunt both versions. She admits that she told the lender he would be earning soon. They call reception together and ask for a written explanation. The answer is another deadline, not a clarification, so Denis does not commit.

They must now plan for the borrowed money without counting on the advertised wage. His aunt asks to be included in the next application earlier. Denis agrees, then adds that enthusiasm cannot make two different employers the same employer. She laughs once, tiredly, and keeps both forms.

company--check.title: Outside the queue
company--check.summary: Denis leaves with the neighbour, his passport and copies of the changed contract. He gives reception no fee. They start checking the agency
paragraphs: Denis leaves with the neighbour, his passport and copies of the changed contract. He gives reception no fee. They start checking the agency and promised employer through independent official contacts rather than the number printed in the advert.

The deadline passes while they wait for answers. Denis tells his aunt they have not verified the offer and will not treat a queue as proof. She asks how to repay the loan. He offers part of his savings and helps her speak to the lender about dates, without promising money from a job he has not taken.

The neighbour sends him another vacancy to investigate later. It is not a replacement guaranteed by this decision. Denis is disappointed, relieved and embarrassed in alternating minutes. He keeps the conflicting contract as part of the record, not as a ticket he has already lost.

company--family.title: A call with the contract open
company--family.summary: Denis puts his aunt on speaker with her permission and reads the hotel advert beside the domestic-work contract. The neighbour explains the
paragraphs: Denis puts his aunt on speaker with her permission and reads the hotel advert beside the domestic-work contract. The neighbour explains the deductions she noticed, without claiming the whole agency has been verified. His aunt asks reception directly which job he would actually do.

Reception cannot supply matching written terms before closing. Denis keeps his passport and leaves without paying. His aunt is angry about the pressure but also about the loan she took before seeing any contract. Denis admits he encouraged her with the advert.

At home they write a repayment plan using money they actually have. It postpones a household purchase and several journeys Denis wanted to make. The job search continues with his aunt involved in reading offers, a slower arrangement that tonight costs both of them a difficult conversation.

delay--facts.title: A pause with a price
delay--facts.summary: Denis sends his aunt photographs of the conflicting job descriptions and says he has kept his passport and paid nothing. He asks to pause un
paragraphs: Denis sends his aunt photographs of the conflicting job descriptions and says he has kept his passport and paid nothing. He asks to pause until the agency and offer can be independently verified. She agrees, after asking twice whether the hotel job might still be real.

The office says his place is gone. That does not settle the verification question; it settles tonight’s deadline. Denis and his aunt contact the lender and explain that the expected work is not confirmed. They still owe the loan, with repayment starting from their existing resources.

Denis spends the evening comparing details rather than packing. His aunt brings tea and asks to see the original advert. She had been carrying an imagined departure date. Now they are both looking at the same unfinished application.

delay--extension.title: No matching offer
delay--extension.summary: Having kept his passport, Denis requests an extension in writing and says he needs a contract matching the advertised hotel role. Reception
paragraphs: Having kept his passport, Denis requests an extension in writing and says he needs a contract matching the advertised hotel role. Reception repeats that the place expires at five. They do not provide a matching offer. Denis leaves with his documents and does not pay.

He tells his aunt he tried to preserve the opportunity while asking for clear terms, and could not obtain both. She wishes he had called earlier. He wishes the advert had been accurate. Neither wish pays the loan, so they work out the first instalment from his savings and her next income.

He saves the messages for independent checking. The next morning he goes back to a local job application he had nearly abandoned. It is not the journey he imagined. The passport remains ready for an offer he can actually read from beginning to end.

opening.title: The Road Has Disappeared
opening.summary: The assessment starts in twenty minutes. Floodwater has swallowed the route.
paragraphs: Patricia stops at the edge of the flooded lane in Bwaise. Water covers the drain and the place where the path used to turn. Her younger brother squeezes her hand. Their morning school assessment starts in twenty minutes.

Patricia is sixteen. A neighbour says the longer route may still be open, but cannot see its far end. Her mother has already reached work and cannot leave her shift. A boda rider shakes his head at the water and turns back.
They are standing on dry ground outside a shop. Patricia’s phone has enough airtime for one short call.
Their neighbour Uncle Rwamiti is helping nearby households move things out of the water.

choices.label: Ask about a longer dry route and check it before taking your brother.
Stay on dry ground and call school for guidance about arrival and the assessment.
Take your brother home by a confirmed dry route and contact your mother.

route.title: The late arrival
route.summary: Patricia asks a shopkeeper about the alternative and waits while he phones someone at its far end. A dry route is confirmed, but it takes fo
paragraphs: Patricia asks a shopkeeper about the alternative and waits while he phones someone at its far end. A dry route is confirmed, but it takes forty minutes. She and her brother use it, stopping again where a side lane has water rather than guessing what lies beneath it.

At the school gate the assessment has started. Her brother’s class is in another building and he is frightened to go alone. The guard says Patricia must report to the office before entering her own room. She cannot do both immediately.

Uncle Rwamiti is delivering a repaired chair to the office. Seeing the pair, he carries the chair behind them instead of offering a shortcut. “This chair is late too. Fortunately, it has no marks to lose.” The guard can call her brother’s class teacher while Patricia explains their arrival.

choices.label: Ask for an adult handover for your brother, then report your own delay.
Stay together in the office until staff arrange both next steps.

contact.title: The bell elsewhere
contact.summary: Patricia calls from the shop. The school says the assessment has started and asks them to avoid the flooded route. An alternative may be ava
paragraphs: Patricia calls from the shop. The school says the assessment has started and asks them to avoid the flooded route. An alternative may be available later; for now, staff record where the children are waiting and ask Patricia to update them.

Her mother calls back but cannot leave work. She can contact a trusted neighbour who may collect her brother. Patricia does not know whether the school will allow a later sitting; staying safe has not solved that question.

Uncle Rwamiti is helping the shopkeeper move sacks above the wet floor inside. He clears a dry bench for the children. “My beans have excellent attendance today,” he mutters, struggling with a sack. The neighbour rings to say she can arrive in fifteen minutes. The school needs an update.

choices.label: Arrange the trusted neighbour’s handover with your mother and update school.
Tell school you will take your brother home by a confirmed dry route.

home.title: The assessment continues
home.summary: Patricia asks the shopkeeper to confirm a dry way back and takes her brother home. Her mother answers from work and agrees they should stay
paragraphs: Patricia asks the shopkeeper to confirm a dry way back and takes her brother home. Her mother answers from work and agrees they should stay there while conditions are uncertain. She cannot come home until her shift ends.

A classmate messages that the assessment is underway. The teacher has marked Patricia absent and knows nothing yet about the blocked lane. Her brother asks whether she will be punished because of him. She tells him the water blocked both of them.

Uncle Rwamiti, their neighbour, calls while checking which households need help moving things. He asks whether they have reached home, then waits while Patricia looks for the school number. “Tell them the journey,” he says, “before the attendance book writes its own.” She has enough charge for one more call.

choices.label: Call the school office now with the route and ask how to arrange a review.
Send a concise account through the class representative and follow up tomorrow.

route--handover.title: Two arrivals recorded
route--handover.summary: After taking the confirmed dry route, Patricia asks the guard to contact her brother’s class teacher. She waits until the teacher takes him
paragraphs: After taking the confirmed dry route, Patricia asks the guard to contact her brother’s class teacher. She waits until the teacher takes him before reporting her own arrival to the office. She explains the route they could not use and the time the alternative took.

She enters the assessment late with less time than her classmates. The teacher records the delay and says any request for an adjustment must follow the school’s procedure. Patricia answers what she can; there is no automatic perfect score for a difficult journey.

At lunch her brother finds her and proudly reports that he did not cry in class. Patricia says the guard almost had to admit a chair to the assessment as well. Before going home they check with school staff and their mother about a safe route. This morning’s solution is not assumed to work again.

route--office.title: Waiting together
route--office.summary: Patricia keeps her brother with her and reports to the office, explaining that she cannot leave him without a handover. Staff contact his te
paragraphs: Patricia keeps her brother with her and reports to the office, explaining that she cannot leave him without a handover. Staff contact his teacher and record why both arrived late. The wait uses more of Patricia’s assessment time.

By the time her brother is collected, her assessment has ended. She asks about a make-up sitting and is told the teacher must review her recorded absence first. She phones her mother with the office’s help, giving the actual route and arrival times rather than saying simply that she missed school.

She returns to lessons with an unresolved assessment, not an invented excuse. Her brother waves from his doorway. After school Patricia asks for the review date in writing, then checks the journey home. Staying together cost time today; it also means she knows exactly who received him.

contact--neighbour.title: A named handover
contact--neighbour.summary: Patricia confirms the neighbour’s arrangement with her mother, then waits on dry ground until she arrives. Her brother goes with the neighbo
paragraphs: Patricia confirms the neighbour’s arrangement with her mother, then waits on dry ground until she arrives. Her brother goes with the neighbour only after Patricia checks where they are going. Patricia updates school with the handover and their morning’s timeline.

When a longer dry route is confirmed, Patricia reaches school after the assessment. She asks about a make-up sitting using the absence already recorded. The teacher schedules a review rather than promising an immediate replacement. Patricia stays for the remaining lessons.

Her mother phones during the lunch break to confirm her brother is home. Patricia sends the review date and asks for help planning tomorrow’s route. The missed assessment is now a specific problem for school to address, while her brother’s location is no longer a guess.

contact--home.title: An absence with a record
contact--home.summary: Having contacted school from the shop, Patricia calls her mother back and agrees to take her brother home. The shopkeeper checks a dry route
paragraphs: Having contacted school from the shop, Patricia calls her mother back and agrees to take her brother home. The shopkeeper checks a dry route with a neighbour before they set off. Patricia updates school instead of vanishing after the first call.

At home she sends the time they arrived and asks how to request a make-up assessment. The answer is a review the next school day. Her brother starts revising beside her, then falls asleep over a page. Her mother cannot leave work, but calls again when she gets a break.

Patricia has missed the morning and will need to catch up on lessons as well as the assessment. She writes down the questions for the review. Before tomorrow, the family checks local conditions again. A dry route this afternoon is useful information, not a promise about the next rain.

home--call.title: The call before the battery dies
home--call.summary: After bringing her brother home, Patricia calls the office and explains where the route was blocked, how they returned and where they are no
paragraphs: After bringing her brother home, Patricia calls the office and explains where the route was blocked, how they returned and where they are now. She asks for the absence to include that account and for the process to request another assessment opportunity.

The office records the call. The teacher will review it tomorrow; no replacement mark is promised. Patricia asks a classmate for the lessons she missed and works through what she can while her brother eats breakfast for the second time.

Her mother brings the review date into their plan for the next morning. Patricia will still need to explain the missed work face to face. Her brother offers to carry her exercise books as compensation. She gives him one light book and keeps the responsibility for the rest.

home--message.title: A message reaches school
home--message.summary: Patricia messages the class representative after returning home, giving the blocked route, safe return and her mother’s contact. She asks th
paragraphs: Patricia messages the class representative after returning home, giving the blocked route, safe return and her mother’s contact. She asks the representative to pass it to the office and confirm delivery. The confirmation arrives before her battery dies.

The message explains the absence but does not itself arrange another assessment. At the next safe opportunity, Patricia and her mother follow up directly with school and request a review. The teacher asks for the full timeline and sets a date to discuss missed work.

Patricia spends the evening catching up from a friend’s notes. Her brother checks every few minutes whether he caused the problem. She repeats that he did not. The family now needs a journey plan and the school’s decision; forwarding a message has started that work, not finished it.

opening.title: I Said I’m Fine
opening.summary: The talent show needs its emcee. Allan cannot get past his bedroom door.
paragraphs: Allan’s phone rings for the fourth time. Outside his bedroom window, someone tests a speaker for the neighbourhood talent show in Mbarara. He is supposed to be the emcee. His shirt is on, his cue cards are ready, and he cannot make himself leave the room.
He is seventeen. He has slept badly and has been struggling through ordinary days for a while. His friend Doreen texts, “Are you too important for us now?” He types “I’m fine”, then deletes it.
The first performer starts in fifteen minutes. Doreen is calling again.
Uncle Rwamiti is helping the organisers and returning an extension lead to Allan’s aunt.

choices.label: Ask Doreen to find a replacement emcee for tonight.
Tell your aunt privately that you are struggling and ask her to stay with you.
Tell Doreen you can try attending only if someone else takes the microphone.

cover.title: The empty microphone
cover.summary: Allan asks Doreen to find a replacement and says he cannot do tonight. He gives no reason. She replies that everyone has worked hard and he
paragraphs: Allan asks Doreen to find a replacement and says he cannot do tonight. He gives no reason. She replies that everyone has worked hard and he could at least turn up. Then she stops calling. He has taken the microphone off his shoulders, but she reads the withdrawal as disdain.
The show begins late with someone else presenting. Allan hears the applause through the window and feels relief mixed with shame. Cancelling has not made the difficult feeling disappear.

Uncle Rwamiti, returning a borrowed extension lead, knocks and leaves it with Allan’s aunt. He sends Allan a message: “The new emcee has introduced the drummer twice. The drummer is enjoying the promotion. Want company, or quiet?” Doreen sends a photograph of the empty chair they saved for him.

choices.label: Tell Doreen a little of what is happening and ask for a quiet conversation later.
Accept Uncle Rwamiti’s offer of quiet company and leave the friendship discussion for tomorrow.

trusted.title: One person knows
trusted.summary: Allan tells his aunt he cannot get himself out of the room and has been finding days difficult lately. She sits down instead of telling him
paragraphs: Allan tells his aunt he cannot get himself out of the room and has been finding days difficult lately. She sits down instead of telling him to hurry. With his agreement, she calls the organiser to say he cannot present tonight, without explaining his private situation.

Doreen hears that Allan’s aunt cancelled for him and thinks he is avoiding her. She sends, “You could have told me yourself.” Allan has support at home, but someone outside has filled the gap in the explanation.

Uncle Rwamiti arrives with the event’s missing extension lead. His aunt asks him to leave it at the door. He does, then texts Allan a picture of the drummer waiting for electricity: “This one actually can blame the cable.” Allan’s aunt asks whether he wants help answering Doreen or would rather rest first.

choices.label: Send Doreen your own brief explanation while keeping the details private.
Ask your aunt to help arrange support and leave Doreen a time to talk tomorrow.

smaller.title: At the edge of the show
smaller.summary: Doreen finds a replacement, and Allan comes with his aunt as far as the chairs at the edge of the show. He is not the emcee. The music feels
paragraphs: Doreen finds a replacement, and Allan comes with his aunt as far as the chairs at the edge of the show. He is not the emcee. The music feels too loud. He sits down before anybody can hand him the cue cards back.

Doreen says she thought he was avoiding the whole neighbourhood. Now she asks why he could come but would not present. Attending has made him visible, while leaving the reason for the changed role unexplained.

Uncle Rwamiti points to two chairs farther from the speaker. “These seats are for people who appreciate the drummer from a distance.” Allan moves with his aunt. Doreen offers him the microphone for just one introduction. His original agreement was that somebody else would use it.

choices.label: Keep the smaller role and explain privately that the stage is too much tonight.
Tell Doreen you need to go home and leave with your aunt.

cover--explain.title: A smaller explanation
cover--explain.summary: Having asked for cover, Allan tells Doreen he has been struggling and could not face the stage tonight. He says he is not ready to explain e
paragraphs: Having asked for cover, Allan tells Doreen he has been struggling and could not face the stage tonight. He says he is not ready to explain everything, but asks her not to interpret the empty chair as contempt. She replies that she was hurt and wishes he had told her earlier.

They agree to speak after the show without the event group listening. Allan asks his aunt to sit with him meanwhile. She listens and helps him plan a conversation with a qualified health professional about the difficulties that have been continuing.

Doreen brings the unused cue cards back. Allan laughs at a spelling mistake he had meant to fix, then becomes quiet again. The evening contains both moments. There is no announcement that he is better, and the next conversation now has somebody willing to attend it with him.

cover--company.title: Two chairs at home
cover--company.summary: After arranging a replacement, Allan asks Uncle Rwamiti to sit with him quietly. He tells his aunt where they will be and asks her to join l
paragraphs: After arranging a replacement, Allan asks Uncle Rwamiti to sit with him quietly. He tells his aunt where they will be and asks her to join later. They stay at home while the show continues; Allan does not force himself to attend as proof that he cares.

Uncle Rwamiti brings tea, misplaces a spoon and spends several minutes looking for the spoon he is holding. Allan smiles once. The smile does not cancel the difficulty. When his aunt joins them, he tells her he has been struggling for more than tonight and asks for help finding appropriate support.

Next morning Allan messages Doreen with a brief explanation and an apology for leaving the plan so late. She is still annoyed about the scramble. They arrange to talk. He has accepted company and postponed a difficult conversation, rather than settled everything in one evening.

trusted--answer.title: His own message
trusted--answer.summary: Having told his aunt, Allan sends Doreen a message in his own words: he is struggling, cannot present tonight and is grateful she is helping
paragraphs: Having told his aunt, Allan sends Doreen a message in his own words: he is struggling, cannot present tonight and is grateful she is helping cover. He asks to discuss it privately another day. He does not ask his aunt to invent an illness or speak for him again.

Doreen replies that she mistook the silence for arrogance. She still wants more notice if plans change. Allan agrees, without promising he can predict every difficult day. His aunt helps him arrange appropriate professional support for what has been continuing.

They eat at home with the talent show audible in the distance. Allan puts the cue cards away rather than tearing them up. Tomorrow does not have to include a microphone, but it does include a person who knows how tonight actually went.

trusted--rest.title: Tonight without the stage
trusted--rest.summary: Allan tells his aunt he needs rest before explaining more to Doreen. He sends a short message offering a private call tomorrow and saying to
paragraphs: Allan tells his aunt he needs rest before explaining more to Doreen. He sends a short message offering a private call tomorrow and saying tonight’s withdrawal is not about being too important for the show. His aunt helps him look for appropriate professional support.

Doreen replies with a time, not a full reconciliation. The replacement emcee finishes the event. Allan stays home, relieved that the role is covered and still troubled by what made the door feel impossible. His aunt checks what company he wants rather than deciding the evening for him.

In the morning the call happens. Doreen describes the scramble; Allan describes only as much as he is ready to share. They make a smaller plan for the next event. Keeping tonight private has given him room to seek help, while leaving the friendship a real conversation to complete.

smaller--boundary.title: An audience member
smaller--boundary.summary: Having agreed only to attend, Allan declines the single introduction. He tells Doreen privately that he has been struggling and the stage is
paragraphs: Having agreed only to attend, Allan declines the single introduction. He tells Doreen privately that he has been struggling and the stage is too much tonight. He asks her to keep that explanation out of the event group. She accepts and returns to the replacement emcee.

Allan watches two performances from the quieter chairs, then leaves with his aunt. He enjoyed one act and still needed to go. At home he asks her to help him seek appropriate support for the difficult days, rather than treating attendance as evidence that everything is fine.

Doreen texts a photograph of the cue cards on the table, with no demand attached. Allan thanks her for keeping the role covered. The next event remains undecided. Tonight he kept the boundary that made coming possible, and now has a conversation about what support comes next.

smaller--leave.title: A short visit
smaller--leave.summary: Allan declines the microphone and tells Doreen the smaller role is still too much tonight. He leaves with his aunt after the first performan
paragraphs: Allan declines the microphone and tells Doreen the smaller role is still too much tonight. He leaves with his aunt after the first performance. Doreen looks disappointed, then says the replacement can finish. The show continues without requiring his return.

At home, Allan explains to his aunt that this has been building for a while. She helps him plan to seek appropriate professional support. Going outside has not fixed it; going home has not proved he failed. He is tired and wants the cue cards out of sight for now.

The next day he thanks Doreen for covering and offers a private conversation about what happened. She admits she had read his silence as arrogance. Their next plan includes permission to change the role early. It is a practical change, with more talking and support still ahead.

record.confront: Your brother fetches the care note because you asked him to show it, rather than taking his assurance about the date.
record.search: You take the care note from the folder you searched. Your brother sees the photograph you made of the papers and asks why you kept it from him.
record.third: Your aunt sends the carbon copy you requested. You show it to your brother before he brings out the hospital note; he knows you contacted her first.

witness.confront: You ask who heard the agreement. Your brother names your aunt. You call her with him present and ask her to bring her copy.
witness.search: You call the aunt whose name you found on the page. Your brother hears the call from the doorway. She agrees to come.
witness.third: You ask your aunt to come because you want the account heard in front of your brother. He sees her enter before she speaks.

delay.confront: You tell your brother no one should sign in the morning, then make the call to the lawyer in front of him.
delay.search: You put the folder away, keeping the photograph, and call the lawyer before agreeing to let the papers leave the house.
delay.third: You ask your aunt to join a call to the lawyer at dawn. Because the appointment is early, she suggests leaving a joint message now. Your brother hears both of you.

opening.title: The message
opening.summary: The message arrived six months after her funeral.
paragraphs: At 11:43 p.m., your mother’s number sends a voice note. You have kept the contact because deleting it felt too much like admitting she was gone.
The recording begins with the familiar scrape of her chair across the veranda. Then her voice: ‘If your brother tells you I signed it, ask him to show you the page.’
There is a breath, a sound like a door opening, and the recording ends. Your brother is asleep in the next room. Tomorrow the family land changes hands. The papers are already on the table.
Your mother never liked that sale. She also knew how to hold a grudge. You replay the final breath until you cannot tell whether you hear a name or only the rain.

choices.label: Wake your brother and play the recording.
Compare the transfer with the hospital papers.
Call your aunt before anyone signs.

confront.title: Across the table
confront.summary: Your brother sits at the kitchen table while the rain taps the window. He listens once, then asks you to play the final breath again. He doe
paragraphs: Your brother sits at the kitchen table while the rain taps the window. He listens once, then asks you to play the final breath again. He does not reach for the phone.

“I was there,” he says. Your mother wanted treatment and the sale could have paid for it. He pushes the folder toward you. The transfer bears a date two days after the last care discussion recorded in the folder. He says the hospital clerk entered it late.

Your aunt texts before you answer: “I sent that note from Mum’s old handset tonight. The repair shop recovered the recording she made in June. I heard the transfer was tomorrow.” You have a sender to ask about, not a message from the dead.

He wants you to believe the decision was hers. You want to believe he had a reason to hide the paper. Tomorrow the lawyer will ask for both your signatures. Tonight your brother is still sitting across from you.

choices.label: Ask him to show you the hospital record.
Ask who else heard your mother agree.
Tell him nobody signs in the morning.

search.title: Inside the folder
search.summary: The folder is thinner than you remember. Under the transfer is a pharmacy receipt. Beneath it, the corner of a page with your mother’s thumb
paragraphs: The folder is thinner than you remember. Under the transfer is a pharmacy receipt. Beneath it, the corner of a page with your mother’s thumbprint and your aunt’s name as witness.
A blue impression from the signature runs onto the folder. It could be fresh ink from a copied page. It could be nothing. You photograph the order of the papers before lifting the top sheet.

Your aunt texts: “That was me using Mum’s old handset. The repair shop recovered the June recording. I sent it when I heard tomorrow’s date.” The new message has a living sender; the older instruction still needs checking.
Your brother appears in the doorway. He sees the open folder but not the photograph you took. If you keep searching, he may call it an accusation. If you stop, the missing page may never return.

choices.label: Compare the dates against the hospital record.
Call the aunt named on the thumbprint page.
Put the folder away and stop tomorrow’s signing.

third.title: The witness
third.summary: Your aunt answers on the fourth ring. She says she sent the recording from your mother’s repaired handset tonight. It was recorded in June,
paragraphs: Your aunt answers on the fourth ring. She says she sent the recording from your mother’s repaired handset tonight. It was recorded in June, before her death. The faint second voice is hers: she remembers entering the room as your mother finished. She sent it because she heard tomorrow’s transfer date.

She was at the hospital, but nobody asked her to witness a sale. Your mother signed a different page, she says, about keeping the land in both children’s names. She kept a copy because the original stayed with your brother.
Your brother calls from the next room. Your aunt can come tonight. She can also send the copy. Either way, you are about to bring another person into a secret that was kept inside the family.

choices.label: Ask her to come and speak in front of him.
Ask her to send the page before you confront him.
Ask her to call the lawyer with you at dawn.

record.title: Two different pages
record.summary: You place the hospital care note beside the transfer. It records a discussion on 16 June; the transfer is dated 18 June. The extract does no
paragraphs: You place the hospital care note beside the transfer. It records a discussion on 16 June; the transfer is dated 18 June. The extract does not establish whether she could discuss a sale two days later. It establishes a question the family cannot answer from this page alone.

After you ask about the carbon copy, your brother brings the original instruction from his drawer. It says the land should remain in both children’s names, with your mother’s thumbprint and your aunt’s name as witness. He says the later transfer replaced it. She says she witnessed no sale. He places the treatment bill beside them.

You have enough to stop a signature, and not enough to know every motive. Taking the papers outside the family protects the record. It also makes the conflict public before your brother has answered you.

choices.label: Take the originals to the lawyer without warning him.
Show him both pages and ask for the whole account.
Ask an independent clerk to secure both originals.

witness.title: What she signed
witness.summary: Your aunt arrives with a carbon copy wrapped in a plastic shopping bag. She recognizes the thumbprint. Your mother had asked for the land to
paragraphs: Your aunt arrives with a carbon copy wrapped in a plastic shopping bag. She recognizes the thumbprint. Your mother had asked for the land to be held for both of you, she says. She never heard her authorize a sale.

Your brother says the second page was an earlier plan. The treatment costs changed everything. He opens a drawer and brings out a hospital bill he paid himself. For a moment nobody argues. The amount is real, and the original instruction is still in his drawer. You ask him to bring it out. He does, and you put it beside the transfer.
Your aunt will speak on the record if you ask. She also asks you not to make her a weapon in an argument the two of you have avoided since the funeral.

choices.label: Let her hear your brother’s account before deciding.
Record her testimony before anyone meets the lawyer.
Keep her out of it and take the papers yourself.

delay.title: Before nine
delay.summary: You call the lawyer’s office and leave a message: no transfer can proceed tomorrow without examining both pages. The reply comes quickly. Th
paragraphs: You call the lawyer’s office and leave a message: no transfer can proceed tomorrow without examining both pages. The reply comes quickly. The lawyer will hold the appointment, but only if a family member brings the originals by nine.
Your brother hears the message. He says a buyer is waiting and the delay may end the offer. Your aunt says the land will still be there next week. Neither promises the family will be.
You ask your brother for the original instruction and the treatment bill, and your aunt sends her carbon copy to compare. Both original pages are on the table before you decide who will carry them.
You have bought time, but time does not choose for you. Someone must carry the papers into the office, and someone will remember who asked the lawyer to wait.

choices.label: Tell your brother why you made the call.
Ask the lawyer to hold it without naming a suspect.
Give everyone copies and request a neutral review.

ending-filed.title: The official record
ending-filed.summary: You hand over the originals before the office opens. The lawyer suspends the transfer and records the disputed dates. Your brother learns wh
paragraphs: You hand over the originals before the office opens. The lawyer suspends the transfer and records the disputed dates. Your brother learns what you did from a clerk, not from you. He refuses your call that evening.

The land stays in the family while an inquiry begins. You have protected the evidence, but the first official account now belongs to someone outside the house. Your aunt says that may be necessary. She does not say it will be easy to live together afterward.

ending-confronted.title: The conversation
ending-confronted.summary: You lay the two pages beside the hospital bill. Your brother admits he asked your mother about selling while she was weak. He says she nodde
paragraphs: You lay the two pages beside the hospital bill. Your brother admits he asked your mother about selling while she was weak. He says she nodded. He also admits he never told her the price had changed. You do not call him a liar. You do not sign.

The buyer leaves the next morning. Your brother is furious about the lost money; you are furious that he chose the question for both of you. You agree to find another way to settle the hospital debt. That agreement is small, costly, and real.

ending-review.title: The review
ending-review.summary: An independent clerk takes both originals into secure custody, gives each of you copies and logs the handover. The transfer is paused pendin
paragraphs: An independent clerk takes both originals into secure custody, gives each of you copies and logs the handover. The transfer is paused pending a review. Your brother resents the implication. Your aunt resents being asked for a thumbprint she thought was already enough.

A week later the review finds no recorded discussion authorising the changed price on the later transfer. The family does not agree to proceed on that incomplete record. It cannot tell you what she would have chosen before that day. The land stays unsold. The family must decide what to do with a truth that does not settle every debt.

ending-family.title: In the same room
ending-family.summary: Your aunt listens while your brother explains the treatment bill. She tells him she would have helped if he had asked. He says he believed h
paragraphs: Your aunt listens while your brother explains the treatment bill. She tells him she would have helped if he had asked. He says he believed he had no time. Neither changes what the document says.

The three of you go to the lawyer together and postpone the sale. For the first time since the funeral, the argument includes everyone it affects. The debt remains. So does the house. Trust has not returned, but nobody else gets to decide what your mother meant in a closed room.

ending-witness.title: Her statement
ending-witness.summary: Your aunt gives a signed account of the page she witnessed. The lawyer cannot complete the transfer. Your brother calls her disloyal; she sa
paragraphs: Your aunt gives a signed account of the page she witnessed. The lawyer cannot complete the transfer. Your brother calls her disloyal; she says she owed loyalty to the woman who asked her to be there.

At home you put the voice note beside her statement. Two records now exist, and neither says why your brother kept the second page out of sight. You have made the silence harder to maintain. You have also asked your aunt to carry a part of the conflict that was yours.

ending-paused.title: Seven days
ending-paused.summary: The lawyer agrees to hold the papers for seven days. The buyer moves on. Your brother says you cost the family its only clear way to pay the
paragraphs: The lawyer agrees to hold the papers for seven days. The buyer moves on. Your brother says you cost the family its only clear way to pay the bill. Your aunt offers to help, but she cannot promise enough.

For one week no one signs, sells or forgives. You use the time to find another route through the debt and to ask your brother why he kept the page apart from the transfer. The pause protects the land. It does not spare you the price of uncertainty.

wedding-guest.title: Five Minutes Before the Bride Leaves

opening.title: Five minutes
opening.summary: The car is waiting. Lydia has not told Daniel what nearly stopped the wedding.
paragraphs: The wedding car is already at the gate when a woman you do not know catches your arm. “Lydia nearly left this morning,” she says. “I was the one who drove her back.”

Across the reception hall, Lydia—your oldest friend—is laughing through the final photographs with Daniel. At breakfast she had phoned you from a taxi stage and said she was afraid of the life everyone had planned for her. You told her to come and speak to Daniel. Then the makeup artist arrived and the call ended.

The woman introduces herself as Namazzi, Lydia’s former supervisor. She holds an envelope addressed to Lydia. It contains an offer for a paid, year-long placement in Kigali, beginning next month. Daniel’s family has been telling guests that the couple will move to Jinja and join their business after the honeymoon.
Namazzi does not ask you to expose Lydia. “The offer closes tomorrow at noon,” she says. “I need to know she received it.” Daniel calls Lydia toward the car. Five minutes, perhaps less.
Uncle Rwamiti is helping the driver load gifts.

choices.label: Take Lydia aside and ask what she wants before the car leaves.
Ask Namazzi what happened at the taxi stage.
Ask Daniel what the two of them actually agreed about Jinja.

bride.title: Lydia’s answer
bride.summary: Lydia sees the envelope and stops smiling. She says she wants the placement, and she wants Daniel. She had hoped to tell him before the cere
paragraphs: Lydia sees the envelope and stops smiling. She says she wants the placement, and she wants Daniel. She had hoped to tell him before the ceremony, but his father congratulated her on the Jinja move in front of everyone. Lydia smiled rather than disagree.

“I nearly left because I could not hear my own answer,” she says. She is angry that you told her to speak, then let the day swallow the conversation. Daniel approaches with the car keys. Lydia asks you not to make her decision for her.
The offer closes tomorrow. The car can wait. What kind of help can you give her without taking over?

Uncle Rwamiti has been helping the driver load gifts. He notices the unfinished conversation and returns the last cake box to the hall. “This one has paid for a seat but can wait.” He asks the driver for five minutes. Lydia still has to choose what to say.

choices.label: Give Lydia and Daniel a private five minutes now.
Stay with them if Lydia wants a witness to the conversation.
Let Lydia leave tonight and decide when to speak on her own.

stranger.title: The offer
stranger.summary: Namazzi says Lydia arrived at her office with a small suitcase and asked her to withdraw the offer. She had not told Daniel it existed. When
paragraphs: Namazzi says Lydia arrived at her office with a small suitcase and asked her to withdraw the offer. She had not told Daniel it existed. When Namazzi asked whether Lydia wanted to decline, Lydia said, “I want someone else to stop asking me to.”

Namazzi drove her back, then got the deadline extended to noon tomorrow. She came to the reception because the offer letter had to reach Lydia, not because she wanted a public scene. You can deliver it, leave the decision with Namazzi, or tell Daniel there is an urgent conversation he does not know about.
From the doorway you see Lydia looking for you. She cannot see the envelope behind Namazzi’s back.

Uncle Rwamiti has been helping the driver load gifts. He notices the unfinished conversation and returns the last cake box to the hall. “This one has paid for a seat but can wait.” He asks the driver for five minutes. Lydia still has to choose what to say.

choices.label: Give the sealed offer to Lydia and let her decide what to say.
Ask Namazzi to keep it until Lydia calls her tomorrow morning.
Tell Daniel that Lydia needs to speak to him before they leave.

third.title: What Daniel heard
third.summary: Daniel says he told his family the Jinja plan because he thought it was settled. “She said we would discuss the details after the wedding,”
paragraphs: Daniel says he told his family the Jinja plan because he thought it was settled. “She said we would discuss the details after the wedding,” he says. He hears his own sentence and looks toward Lydia. “Was that not a yes?”
He does not know about Kigali. His father is loading gifts into the car and calling for the couple. Your question has already unsettled Daniel; silence now would not put the evening back as it was.
You know Lydia has an offer, but it is her news. You can make room for a private talk, tell her what Daniel has announced, or step away.

Uncle Rwamiti has been helping the driver load gifts. He notices the unfinished conversation and returns the last cake box to the hall. “This one has paid for a seat but can wait.” He asks the driver for five minutes. Lydia still has to choose what to say.

choices.label: Ask Daniel to give Lydia five minutes alone before the car leaves.
Tell Lydia that Daniel has already announced the Jinja plan.
Step back and let the couple leave without another intervention.

bride_talk.title: The veranda
bride_talk.summary: Lydia asks Daniel to come to the veranda. You hold the door, then leave them there. She tells him about Kigali and about the taxi stage. He
paragraphs: Lydia asks Daniel to come to the veranda. You hold the door, then leave them there. She tells him about Kigali and about the taxi stage. He is hurt that she almost cancelled without telling him why. She is hurt that he turned a discussion into a family announcement.

The car waits twenty minutes. When they return, Daniel tells his father they have not agreed to move to Jinja. His father begins a speech; Lydia says, “Tomorrow, please.” The driver switches off the engine and asks someone to save him a plate.

The next morning Lydia accepts the placement. Daniel has not promised to move, and she has not promised to decline. They have a year to work out what a marriage between two cities would require. It begins with both of them knowing the question.

bride_witness.title: A witness
bride_witness.summary: Lydia asks you to stay. At first Daniel addresses every question to you. You say only that you came because Lydia asked. She takes the envel
paragraphs: Lydia asks you to stay. At first Daniel addresses every question to you. You say only that you came because Lydia asked. She takes the envelope from Namazzi and explains the offer herself.

Daniel admits he told his father about Jinja before Lydia agreed. Lydia admits she kept the placement from him because she feared his answer. Neither apology solves the distance. They tell the driver to wait while they finish a conversation without an audience.

Later Lydia thanks you for standing there and for not speaking for her. Daniel is polite, though he will need longer than an evening to feel included in a plan that almost became a departure. The placement remains open until noon; Lydia leaves with the letter in her own bag.

bride_leave.title: Tomorrow morning
bride_leave.summary: Lydia folds the offer into her handbag and gets into the car. She says she will tell Daniel after they have slept. You let her choose the ti
paragraphs: Lydia folds the offer into her handbag and gets into the car. She says she will tell Daniel after they have slept. You let her choose the timing. Namazzi sends one message: “Noon tomorrow.”

At breakfast Lydia accepts the placement before she speaks to Daniel. When she tells him, he asks why the decision reached Kigali before it reached their table. Lydia says she could not bear to hear another person decide for her. He says he had already done exactly that with Jinja.
They cancel the family lunch and spend the afternoon with two calendars. She has secured the work she wanted. Trust will need more than a deadline to repair.

stranger_letter.title: The envelope
stranger_letter.summary: You give Lydia the sealed envelope. She opens it behind a pillar, reads the deadline, and goes to Daniel. You do not follow. Namazzi starts
paragraphs: You give Lydia the sealed envelope. She opens it behind a pillar, reads the deadline, and goes to Daniel. You do not follow. Namazzi starts toward the gate, then comes back for a slice of cake.
